bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第252巻

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 252.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 252.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀六十八】起上章攝提格，盡柔兆涒灘，凡七年。

translations.literal: [Tang Annals 68] From Shangzhang Shetige through Rouzhao Youtan—seven years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Annals 68] From Shangzhang Shetige through Rouzhao Youtan—seven years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲寅朔，群臣上尊號曰睿文英武明德至仁大聖廣孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiayin, the first day of the month, the officials presented a honorific title: Emperor of Sagacious Culture, Heroic Martiality, Bright Virtue, Supreme Benevolence, Great Sagacity, and Broad Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month (jiayin), the courtiers presented a new honorific: the Emperor of Sagacious Culture, Heroic Martiality, Bright Virtue, Supreme Benevolence, Great Sagacity, and Broad Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: He pardoned the empire.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was declared throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 西川之民聞蠻寇將至，爭走入成都。

translations.literal: The people of Western Shu, hearing that the barbarian raiders were about to arrive, all rushed into Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread through Western Shu that the barbarian armies were coming, people scrambled into Chengdu for safety.

sentences.zh: 時成都但有子城，亦無壕，人所佔地各不過一席許，雨則戴箕盎以自庇。

translations.literal: At the time Chengdu had only the inner citadel and no moat; each person's allotted space was no more than the size of a mat, and when it rained they wore bamboo hats and basins to shelter themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu at the time held only the inner citadel, with no moat. Each refugee had barely room for a sleeping mat; in the rain they sheltered under bamboo hats and bowls turned upside down.

sentences.zh: 又乏水，取摩訶池泥汁，澄而飲之。

translations.literal: Water was also scarce; they took muddy water from Mahā Pool, let it settle, and drank it.
translations.idiomatic: Water ran short as well; people drew muddy water from the Mahā Pool, let it settle, and drank what they could.

sentences.zh: 將士不習武備，節度使盧耽召彭州刺史呉行魯使攝參謀，與前瀘州刺史楊慶-{復}-共修守備，選將校，分職事，立戰棚，具砲檑，造器備，嚴警邏。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers were unpracticed in military preparations. Military Commissioner Lu Dan summoned Pengzhou Prefect Wu Xinglu to serve as acting staff officer; together with former Luzhou Prefect Yang Qingfu they repaired the defenses, selected commanders, divided duties, erected fighting sheds, prepared catapults and rams, manufactured weapons and equipment, and tightened frontier alerts.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison was ill-trained for war. Commissioner Lu Dan called Pengzhou prefect Wu Xinglu to serve as acting staff officer and, with former Luzhou prefect Yang Qingfu, set about fortifying the city: picking officers, assigning duties, building fighting platforms, readying catapults and battering rams, forging arms, and tightening the watch along the approaches.

sentences.zh: 先是，西川將士多虚職名，亦無稟給。

translations.literal: Previously, many officers and soldiers of Western Shu held nominal posts only and received no rations.
translations.idiomatic: Until then many Western Shu soldiers held hollow titles on the rolls and drew no pay or rations.

sentences.zh: 至是，掲榜募驍勇之士，補以實職，厚給糧賜，應募者-{雲}-集。

translations.literal: At this time they posted notices recruiting bold warriors, gave them substantive posts, and granted generous grain and rewards; applicants gathered like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Now they posted notices calling for the brave, gave real commissions to those who came forward, and paid them generously in grain and bounty—and volunteers gathered in swarms.

sentences.zh: 慶-{復}-乃諭之曰：「汝曹皆軍中子弟，年少材勇，平居無由自進，今蠻寇憑陵，乃汝曹取富貴之秋也，可不勉乎！」

translations.literal: Qingfu then addressed them, saying: "You are all sons of military families—young, talented, and brave. In ordinary times you have no way to advance yourselves. Now the barbarian raiders are pressing upon us—this is your season to win wealth and honor. Will you not strive?"
translations.idiomatic: Qingfu rallied them: "You are all sons of the army—young, able, and bold. In peacetime you had no path to rise. Now the barbarians are upon us—this is your chance for rank and reward. Will you not give your utmost?"

sentences.zh: 皆歡呼踴躍。

translations.literal: They all cheered and leaped for joy.
translations.idiomatic: They answered with shouts and leapt in excitement.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是列兵械-{於}-庭，使之各試所能，兩兩角勝，察其勇怯而進退之，得選兵三千人，號曰「突將」。

translations.literal: Thereupon they arrayed weapons in the courtyard and had each man demonstrate his skill, pairing them to contest until one prevailed, observing courage and cowardice to promote or dismiss them; they selected three thousand troops and called them the "Shock Corps."
translations.idiomatic: They then lined weapons in the courtyard and had each man prove himself in paired trials, promoting the bold and weeding out the timid until three thousand were chosen and named the Shock Corps.

sentences.zh: 行魯，彭州人也。

translations.literal: Xinglu was a native of Pengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xinglu was from Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊午，蠻至眉州，耽遣同節度副使王偃等繼書見其用事之臣杜元忠，與之約和。

translations.literal: On wuwu the barbarians reached Meizhou. Dan sent Associate Military Commissioner Wang Yan and others with repeated letters to meet their powerful minister Du Yuanzhong and negotiate peace with him.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the invaders reached Meizhou. Dan sent his deputy Wang Yan with repeated missives to Du Yuanzhong, the man who held real power among them, seeking terms.

sentences.zh: 蠻報曰：「我輩行止，只-{系}-雅懷。」

translations.literal: The barbarians replied: "Our movements depend solely on your gracious intent."
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians replied: "Our movements depend entirely on your gracious intent."

sentences.zh: 路巖、韋保衡上言：「康承訓討龐勳時，逗橈不進，又不能盡其-{餘}-黨，又貪虜獲，不時上功。」

translations.literal: Lu Yan and Wei Baoheng submitted a memorial: "When Kang Chengxun campaigned against Pang Xun, he dallied and would not advance, failed to exterminate the remaining partisans, and moreover was greedy for captives and booty, not reporting achievements in timely fashion."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yan and Wei Baoheng memorialized the throne: "In the campaign against Pang Xun, Kang Chengxun hung back and would not press the attack, left surviving rebels at large, and hoarded captives and loot instead of reporting victories promptly."

sentences.zh: 辛酉，貶蜀王傅、分司，尋再貶恩州司馬。

translations.literal: On xinyou he was demoted to Tutor of the Prince of Shu and assigned to a nominal post in the capital; soon after he was demoted again to military adjutant of Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou he was stripped of rank, made tutor to the Prince of Shu with a nominal capital post, and soon after demoted again to adjutant at Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 南詔進軍新津，定邊之北境也。

translations.literal: Nanzhao advanced on Xinjin, the northern border of Dingbian.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao marched on Xinjin, the northern edge of the Dingbian command.

sentences.zh: 盧耽遣同節度副使譚奉祀致書-{於}-杜元忠，問其所以來之意。

translations.literal: Lu Dan sent Associate Military Commissioner Tan Fengsi with a letter to Du Yuanzhong to ask the purpose of their coming.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dan sent his deputy Tan Fengsi with a letter to Du Yuanzhong asking why they had come.

sentences.zh: 蠻留之不還。

translations.literal: The barbarians detained him and did not return him.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians held him and would not send him back.

sentences.zh: 耽遣使告急-{於}-朝，且請遣使與和，以紓一時之患。

translations.literal: Dan sent envoys to report the emergency to court and also requested that an envoy be sent to make peace, to relieve the immediate peril.
translations.idiomatic: Dan dispatched messengers to the capital with urgent word and asked that an imperial envoy be sent to negotiate peace and ease the immediate crisis.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命知四方館事、太-{僕}-卿支詳爲宣諭通和使。

translations.literal: The court appointed Zhi Xiang, Director of the Bureau of Foreign Affairs and Grand Master of the Imperial Stud, as Commissioner for Proclamation and Reconciliation.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Zhi Xiang, overseer of the Bureau of Foreign Affairs and Grand Master of the Imperial Stud, commissioner to proclaim peace and negotiate terms.

sentences.zh: 蠻以耽待之恭，亦爲之盤桓，而成都守備由是粗完。

translations.literal: Because the barbarians saw that Dan treated them with respect, they too lingered, and thereby the defenses of Chengdu were roughly completed.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by Dan's courtesy, the invaders lingered as well, buying time until Chengdu's defenses were at least roughly in place.

sentences.zh: 甲子，蠻長驅而北，陷雙流。

translations.literal: On jiazi the barbarians drove swiftly north and captured Shuangliu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi they swept north in a long drive and took Shuangliu.

sentences.zh: 庚午，耽遣節度副使柳槃往見之，杜元忠授槃書一通，曰：「此通和之-{後}-，驃信與軍府相見之儀也。」

translations.literal: On gengwu Dan sent Military Commissioner Deputy Liu Pan to meet them. Du Yuanzhong gave Pan one document, saying: "This sets forth the protocol for how the Piao Xin and the military headquarters shall meet after peace is concluded."
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Dan sent his deputy Liu Pan to parley. Du Yuanzhong handed him a document: "This lays out how the Piao Xin and the commandery shall meet once peace is made."

sentences.zh: 其儀以王者自處，語極驕慢。

translations.literal: The protocol treated himself as a king, and the language was extremely arrogant and insolent.
translations.idiomatic: The terms treated the Nanzhao ruler as an equal sovereign, and the tone was brazenly contemptuous.

sentences.zh: 又遣人負彩幕至城南，-{雲}-欲張陳蜀王廳以居驃信。

translations.literal: They also sent men carrying colored awnings to the south of the city, saying they wished to pitch the Hall of the Prince of Shu for the Piao Xin to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent bearers with colored canopies to the south gate, announcing that they meant to set up the Prince of Shu's hall for the Piao Xin to occupy.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，廢定邊軍，-{復}-以七州歸西川。

translations.literal: On guiyou the Dingbian Army was abolished, and the seven prefectures were restored to Western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the court abolished the Dingbian command and returned its seven prefectures to Western Shu.

sentences.zh: 是日，蠻軍抵成都城下。

translations.literal: That same day the barbarian army reached the foot of Chengdu's walls.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the barbarian host came up to the walls of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 前一日，盧耽遣先鋒-{游}-弈使王晝至漢州詗援軍，且趣之。

translations.literal: The day before, Lu Dan had sent Vanguard Envoy Wang Zhou to Hanzhou to scout for relief troops and urge them forward.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, Lu Dan had sent his vanguard envoy Wang Zhou to Hanzhou to learn where the relief columns were and hurry them on.

sentences.zh: 時興元六千人、鳳翔四千人已至漢州，會竇滂以忠武、義成、徐宿四千人自導江奔漢州，就援軍以自存。

translations.literal: At the time six thousand from Xingyuan and four thousand from Fengxiang had already reached Hanzhou; they met Dou Pang, who with four thousand from Zhongwu, Yicheng, Xu, and Su had fled from Daojiang to Hanzhou, joining the relief army to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand men from Xingyuan and four thousand from Fengxiang were already at Hanzhou when Dou Pang arrived with four thousand from Zhongwu, Yicheng, Xu, and Su, having fled Daojiang to throw in with the relief force and save his own skin.

sentences.zh: 丁-{丑}-，王晝以興元、資、簡兵三千-{餘}-人軍-{於}-毘橋，遇蠻前鋒，與戰不利，退保漢州。

translations.literal: On dingchou Wang Zhou led more than three thousand troops from Xingyuan, Zi, and Jian and encamped at Piqiao; they met the barbarian vanguard, fought unsuccessfully, and withdrew to defend Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Wang Zhou marched more than three thousand troops from Xingyuan, Zi, and Jian to camp at Piqiao, clashed with the barbarian van, lost the fight, and fell back to Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時成都日望援軍之至，而竇滂自以失地，欲西川相繼陷沒以分其責。

translations.literal: At the time Chengdu daily awaited the arrival of relief troops, while Dou Pang, blaming himself for losing territory, wished for Western Shu to fall in succession so as to share his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu waited day after day for relief, while Dou Pang—who had lost ground—hoped the rest of Western Shu would collapse as well so his own blame would be diluted.

sentences.zh: 毎援軍自北至，輒説之曰：「蠻衆多-{於}-官軍數十倍，官軍遠來疲弊，未易遽前。」

translations.literal: Whenever relief troops arrived from the north he would tell them: "The barbarian host is many times greater than the government army—tenfold or more. The government troops have come from afar, weary and spent; it is not easy to advance quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a relief column came down from the north he would tell them: "The barbarians outnumber us ten to one. Your men are worn out from the march—it is no time to rush forward."

sentences.zh: 諸將信之，皆狐疑不進。

translations.literal: The generals believed him and all hesitated in doubt, not advancing.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders believed him and hung back in indecision.

sentences.zh: 成都十將李自孝陰與蠻通，欲焚城東倉爲内應，城中執而殺之。

translations.literal: Li Zixiao, a commander of the Chengdu garrison, secretly communicated with the barbarians and planned to burn the eastern granary as an inside signal; the city seized and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zixiao, a Chengdu officer, had secretly contacted the barbarians and plotted to burn the eastern granary as a signal from within; the city seized him and put him to death.

sentences.zh: -{後}-數日，蠻果攻城，久之，城中無應而止。

translations.literal: Several days later the barbarians indeed assaulted the city; after a long time, with no response inside, they ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the barbarians did assault the walls, but after a long wait with no signal from within, they gave up.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸未朔，蠻合梯-{沖}-四-{面}-攻成都，城上以鉤繯挽之使近，投火沃油焚之，攻者皆死。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guiwei, the first day, the barbarians combined scaling ladders and battering rams and attacked Chengdu on four sides; atop the walls they used hooked ropes to draw the ladders near, poured fire and oil to burn them, and all the attackers died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day (guiwei), the barbarians assaulted Chengdu from all sides with ladders and rams. Defenders hauled the ladders in with grappling hooks, drenched them in fire and boiling oil, and every man on them perished.

sentences.zh: 盧耽以楊慶-{復}-、攝左都押牙李驤各帥突將出戰，殺傷蠻二千-{餘}-人，會暮，焚其攻具三千-{餘}-物而還。

translations.literal: Lu Dan had Yang Qingfu and Acting Left Chief Military Adjutant Li Zang each lead the Shock Corps out to battle, killing and wounding more than two thousand barbarians; at dusk they burned more than three thousand pieces of siege equipment and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dan sent Yang Qingfu and acting adjutant Li Zang, each leading the Shock Corps, in a sortie that killed or wounded more than two thousand barbarians; at dusk they burned over three thousand siege engines and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蜀人素怯，其突將新爲慶-{復}-所獎拔，且利-{於}-厚賞，勇氣自倍，其不得出者，皆憤郁求奮。

translations.literal: The people of Shu were by nature timid; the Shock Corps, newly encouraged and promoted by Qingfu and moreover tempted by generous rewards, doubled their courage of themselves, while those who could not go out all chafed in resentment, begging to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Shu men were known for timidity, but the Shock Corps—freshly rallied by Qingfu and hungry for the rich rewards on offer—fought with redoubled spirit, while those left behind seethed with envy and begged for their turn.

sentences.zh: -{後}-數日，賊取民籬，重沓濕而屈之，以爲蓬，置人其下，舉以抵城而斸之，矢石不能入，火不能然。

translations.literal: Several days later the rebels took the people's fences, layered them wet and bent them into shelters, placed men beneath, and raised them against the wall to dig at it; arrows and stones could not penetrate, and fire could not set them ablaze.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the attackers took civilian fences, soaked and bent them into covered shelters, and pushed them against the wall with diggers underneath—arrows and stones could not pierce them, nor could fire set them alight.

sentences.zh: 慶-{復}-溶鐵汁以灌之，攻者又死。

translations.literal: Qingfu melted iron and poured it over them, and the attackers died again.
translations.idiomatic: Qingfu poured molten iron over them, and the attackers died again.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，支詳遣使與蠻約和。

translations.literal: On yiyou Zhi Xiang sent envoys to negotiate peace with the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Zhi Xiang sent envoys to treat for peace with the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，蠻斂兵請和。

translations.literal: On dinghai the barbarians drew in their troops and requested peace.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the barbarians pulled back their lines and asked for peace.

sentences.zh: 戊子，遣使迎支詳。

translations.literal: On wuzi they sent envoys to welcome Zhi Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi they sent envoys to escort Zhi Xiang forward.

sentences.zh: 時顏慶-{復}-以援軍將至，詳謂蠻使曰：「受詔詣定邊約和，今-{雲}-南乃圍成都，則與向日詔旨異矣。

translations.literal: At the time Yan Qingfu's relief army was about to arrive. Xiang said to the barbarian envoy: "I received orders to go to Dingbian to negotiate peace. Now Yunnan is besieging Chengdu—this differs from the earlier imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qingfu's relief column was nearing. Xiang told the barbarian envoy: "I was ordered to make peace at Dingbian. Yunnan is now besieging Chengdu—that is not what the earlier edict contemplated.

sentences.zh: 且朝廷所以和者，冀其不犯成都也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the reason the court sought peace was in hope that Chengdu would not be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: The court sought peace precisely so that Chengdu would not be attacked.

sentences.zh: 今矢石晝夜相交，何謂和乎！」

translations.literal: Now arrows and stones fly day and night—what is this called peace!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet arrows and stones fly day and night—how can this be called peace!"

sentences.zh: 蠻見和使不至，庚寅，-{復}-進攻城。

translations.literal: When the barbarians saw that the peace envoy did not come, on gengyin they again advanced to assault the city.
translations.idiomatic: When no peace envoy appeared, on gengyin they resumed the assault.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，城中出兵撃之，乃退。

translations.literal: On xinmao the city sent troops out to strike them, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the garrison sallied and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 初，韋皋招南詔以破吐蕃，既而蠻訴以無甲弩，皋使匠往教之，數歳，蠻中甲駑皆精利。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei Gao had recruited Nanzhao to break Tibet; afterward the barbarians complained that they lacked armor and crossbows, and Gao sent craftsmen to teach them; within several years armor and crossbows throughout the barbarian lands were all keen and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Wei Gao had enlisted Nanzhao against Tibet; when they complained of lacking armor and crossbows, he sent craftsmen to train them, and within a few years Nanzhao's arms were as fine as any in the empire.

sentences.zh: 又，東蠻苴那時、勿鄧、夢-{沖}-三部助皋破吐蕃有功。

translations.literal: Moreover, the three Eastern Barbarian tribes of Junashi, Wudeng, and Mengchong had aided Gao in defeating Tibet with merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Barbarian tribes of Junashi, Wudeng, and Mengchong had also fought well for Gao against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 其-{後}-邊吏遇之無狀，東蠻怨唐深，自附-{於}-南詔，毎從南詔入寇，爲之盡力，得唐人，皆虐殺之。

translations.literal: Afterward frontier officials treated them without propriety; the Eastern Barbarians bore deep resentment toward Tang and attached themselves to Nanzhao, each time following Nanzhao in raids and exerting themselves to the utmost; whenever they captured Tang people they all tortured and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Later frontier officials treated them shamefully; the Eastern Barbarians turned against Tang and threw in with Nanzhao, raiding at their side and sparing no effort; every Tang captive they took was butchered with cruelty.

sentences.zh: 朝廷貶竇滂爲康州司戸，以顏慶-{復}-爲東川節度使，凡援蜀諸軍，皆受慶-{復}-節-{制}-。

translations.literal: The court demoted Dou Pang to registrar of Kangzhou and appointed Yan Qingfu Military Commissioner of Dongchuan; all armies aiding Shu were placed under Qingfu's command.
translations.idiomatic: The court demoted Dou Pang to clerk of Kangzhou and made Yan Qingfu commissioner of Dongchuan; every relief army in Shu came under his command.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，慶-{復}-至新都，蠻分兵往拒之。

translations.literal: On guisi Qingfu reached Xindu; the barbarians divided their troops to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Qingfu reached Xindu, and the barbarians sent detachments to block him.

sentences.zh: 甲午，與慶-{復}-遇，慶-{復}-大破蠻軍，殺二千-{餘}-人，蜀民數千人爭操芟刀、白棓以助官軍，呼聲震野。

translations.literal: On jiawu they met Qingfu; Qingfu routed the barbarian army and killed more than two thousand. Several thousand Shu civilians vied to seize sickles and white clubs to aid the government troops, and their shouts shook the fields.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu they met Qingfu, who shattered the barbarian host and killed more than two thousand. Thousands of Shu civilians seized sickles and clubs to join the government troops, and their cheers shook the countryside.

sentences.zh: 乙未，蠻歩騎數萬-{復}-至，會右武衞上將軍宋威以忠武軍二千人至，即與諸軍會戰，蠻軍大敗，死者五千-{餘}-人，退保星宿山。

translations.literal: On yiwei tens of thousands of barbarian infantry and cavalry came again; Right Martial Guard General Song Wei arrived with two thousand from the Zhongwu Army, and at once joined the other armies in battle; the barbarian army was utterly defeated, with more than five thousand dead, and they withdrew to hold Xingsu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei tens of thousands of barbarian foot and horse returned; General Song Wei of the Right Martial Guard arrived with two thousand Zhongwu troops and joined the other columns at once. The barbarians were routed—more than five thousand dead—and fell back to Xingsu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 威進軍沱江驛，距成都三十-{里}-。

translations.literal: Wei advanced his army to Tuojiang Post, thirty li from Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei marched to Tuojiang Post, thirty li from Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 蠻遣其臣楊定保詣支詳請和，詳曰：「宜先解圍退軍。」

translations.literal: The barbarians sent their minister Yang Dingbao to Zhi Xiang to request peace. Xiang said: "You should first lift the siege and withdraw your troops."
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians sent Yang Dingbao to Zhi Xiang to sue for peace. Xiang replied: "Lift the siege and withdraw your army first."

sentences.zh: 定保還，蠻圍城如故。

translations.literal: Dingbao returned, but the barbarian siege of the city remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Dingbao returned, but the siege continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 城中不知援軍之至，但見其數來請和，知援軍必勝矣。

translations.literal: Inside the city they did not know that relief troops had arrived, but seeing the barbarians repeatedly come to request peace, they knew the relief army must prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The city did not yet know relief had come, but when the barbarians kept sending peace envoys, the defenders knew the relief army must be winning.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，蠻-{復}-請和，使者十返，城中亦依違答之。

translations.literal: On wuxu the barbarians again requested peace; envoys came and went ten times, and inside the city they too answered evasively.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the barbarians again sued for peace; envoys shuttled back and forth ten times, and the city answered with deliberate equivocation.

sentences.zh: 蠻以援軍在近，攻城尤急，驃信以下親立矢石之間。

translations.literal: Because relief troops were near, the barbarians pressed the assault all the more fiercely; the Piao Xin and his subordinates personally stood amid flying arrows and stones.
translations.idiomatic: With relief near, the barbarians redoubled the assault; the Piao Xin and his chiefs stood in person amid the hail of arrows and stones.

sentences.zh: 庚子，官軍至城下與蠻戰，奪其陞遷橋，是夕，蠻自燒攻具遁去，比明，官軍乃覺之。

translations.literal: On gengzi the government army reached the foot of the city and fought the barbarians, seizing their Shengqian Bridge. That evening the barbarians burned their siege equipment and fled; only at dawn did the government troops realize it.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the imperial troops fought the barbarians below the walls and took the Shengqian Bridge. That night the invaders burned their engines and slipped away; the garrison did not realize it until dawn.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷使顏慶-{復}-救成都，命宋威屯綿，漢爲-{後}-繼。

translations.literal: Earlier the court had sent Yan Qingfu to rescue Chengdu and ordered Song Wei to hold Mian and Han as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: The court had sent Yan Qingfu to relieve Chengdu and ordered Song Wei to hold Mian and Han as a reserve.

sentences.zh: 威乘勝先至城下，破蠻軍功居多，慶-{復}-疾之。

translations.literal: Wei, riding his victory, reached the city first; he had broken the barbarian army and his achievements were the greatest—Qingfu resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei pressed his advantage and reached the city first, winning the lion's share of the credit—Qingfu took offense.

sentences.zh: 威飯士，欲追蠻軍，城中戰士亦欲與北軍合勢倶進，慶-{復}-牒威，奪其軍，勒歸漢州。

translations.literal: Wei fed his soldiers and wished to pursue the barbarian army; the warriors in the city also wished to join the northern army in combined advance. Qingfu sent a dispatch to Wei, seized his command, and ordered him back to Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had fed his men and meant to pursue; the city's fighters wanted to join the northern columns in a joint pursuit. Qingfu stripped him of command by dispatch and sent him back to Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 蠻至雙流，阻新穿水，造橋未能成，狼狽失度。

translations.literal: The barbarians reached Shuangliu, blocked by the newly dug channel; they could not finish building a bridge and were in disarray beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians reached Shuangliu but were stopped by a newly cut canal; their bridge was unfinished and they fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 三日，橋成，乃得過，斷橋而去，甲兵服物遺棄-{於}-路，蜀人甚恨之。

translations.literal: On the third day the bridge was completed and they were able to cross; they cut the bridge behind them and departed, leaving armor, weapons, and clothing abandoned along the road—the people of Shu hated this deeply.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day the bridge was done and they crossed, then destroyed it behind them. Armor and gear littered the road, and the people of Shu were furious.

sentences.zh: 黎州刺史嚴師本收散卒數千保邛州，蠻圍之，二日，不克，亦-{捨}-去。

translations.literal: Lizhou Prefect Yan Shiben gathered several thousand scattered troops and held Qiongzhou; the barbarians besieged it for two days, could not take it, and also abandoned the effort.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhou prefect Yan Shiben rallied several thousand stragglers at Qiongzhou; the barbarians besieged it two days, failed to take it, and moved on.

sentences.zh: 顏慶-{復}-始教蜀人-{築}-壅門城，穿塹引水滿之，植鹿角，分營舖。

translations.literal: Yan Qingfu began teaching the people of Shu to build barrier-gate cities, dig moats and fill them with water, plant abatis, and divide camps and posts.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qingfu began teaching the Shu to build outer gate fortifications, cut moats and flood them, plant abatis, and lay out camps and posts.

sentences.zh: 蠻知有備，自是不-{復}-犯成都矣。

translations.literal: The barbarians knew there were preparations, and from then on they no longer attacked Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Once the barbarians saw the defenses, they never attacked Chengdu again.

sentences.zh: 先是，西川牙將有職無官，及拒卻南詔，四人以功授監察-{御}-史，堂帖，人輸堂例錢三百緡；

translations.literal: Previously, Western Shu military adjutants held posts without official rank; for repelling Nanzhao, four men were granted the post of Investigating Censor by chancellor's appointment, and each man paid three hundred strings in customary chancellor's-office fees;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, many Western Shu adjutants held duties without formal rank; four who helped repel Nanzhao were made investigating censors by direct appointment, and each had to pay three hundred strings in the usual chancellor's-office fee;

sentences.zh: 貧者苦之。

translations.literal: the poor suffered bitterly from this.
translations.idiomatic: which the poor could scarcely bear.

sentences.zh: 三月，左-{僕}-射、同平章事曹確同平章事，充鎭海節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor Cao Que remained Associate Grand Councillor and was appointed Military Commissioner of Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Vice Director and Grand Councillor Cao Que kept his council seat and was made military commissioner of Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙午，以翰林學士承旨、兵部侍郎韋保衡同平章事。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingwu, Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War Wei Baoheng was made Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on bingwu, Hanlin expositor and Vice Minister of War Wei Baoheng was elevated to grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 徐賊-{餘}-黨猶相聚閭裡爲群盜，散居兗、鄆、靑、齊之間，詔徐州觀察使夏侯瞳招諭之。

translations.literal: Remnants of the Xu rebels still gathered in villages as bandit gangs, scattered among Yan, Yun, Qing, and Qi; an edict ordered Xuzhou Observation Commissioner Xiahou Tong to summon and persuade them.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors of the Xu rebellion still banded together in villages across Yan, Yun, Qing, and Qi; the throne ordered Xuzhou commissioner Xiahou Tong to offer them amnesty and terms.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁-{丑}-，以邛州刺史呉行魯爲西川留-{後}-。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dingchou, Qiongzhou Prefect Wu Xinglu was made Acting Governor of Western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingchou, Qiongzhou prefect Wu Xinglu was named acting governor of Western Shu.

sentences.zh: 光州民逐刺史李弱翁，弱翁奔新息。

translations.literal: The people of Guangzhou drove out Prefect Li Ruoweng; Ruoweng fled to Xinxī.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guangzhou expelled prefect Li Ruoweng, who fled to Xinxī.

sentences.zh: 左補闕楊堪等上言：「刺史不道，百姓負冤，當訴-{於}-朝廷，置諸典刑，豈得群黨相聚，擅自斥逐，亂上下之分！

translations.literal: Left Remonstrance Official Yang Kan and others submitted a memorial: "If a prefect is without the Way and the people bear grievances, they should appeal to the court and have him placed under the penal code—how can mobs gather, on their own authority drive him out, and overturn the distinction between superior and inferior!
translations.idiomatic: Left remonstrance official Yang Kan and others memorialized: "If a prefect is corrupt and the people are wronged, they should appeal to the throne and let the law take its course. How can mobs assemble on their own authority, expel an official, and overturn the order between ruler and subject!

sentences.zh: 此風殆不可長，宜加嚴誅，以懲來者！」

translations.literal: This practice must not be allowed to spread; severe punishment should be imposed to warn those who come after!"
translations.idiomatic: This custom must not be allowed to spread. Severe punishment is needed to warn others!"

sentences.zh: 上令百官議處置徐州之宜。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the officials to deliberate on the proper disposition of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the court to debate how Xuzhou should be governed.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙午，太子少傅李膠等狀，以爲：「徐州雖屢構禍亂，未必比屋頑凶；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingwu, Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent Li Jiao and others submitted a report, stating: "Although Xuzhou has repeatedly stirred up calamity and disorder, it is not necessarily that every household is stubbornly vicious;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingwu, Junior Tutor Li Jiao and others reported: "Though Xuzhou has rebelled again and again, not every household there is irredeemably wicked;

sentences.zh: 蓋由統-{御}-失人，是致-{奸}-回乘釁。

translations.literal: it is rather because control and governance employed the wrong men, which caused treacherous villains to seize the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: the trouble comes from bad leadership, which lets the wicked seize their chance.

sentences.zh: 今使名雖降，兵額尚存，以爲支郡則糧餉不給，分隸別落則人心未服；

translations.literal: now though its title is reduced, its troop quota still remains; if made a subordinate prefecture its grain and pay would not suffice, and if divided and placed under other jurisdictions the people's hearts would not be won;
translations.idiomatic: though its status is reduced, its troop rolls remain; as a subordinate prefecture it could not be fed, and if split among other circuits the people would not accept it;

sentences.zh: 或舊惡相繼，更成披猖。

translations.literal: or old enmities might follow one upon another, leading to even greater rampage.
translations.idiomatic: old grudges might flare again into open revolt.

sentences.zh: 惟泗州向因攻守，結釁已深，宜有更張，庶爲兩便。」

translations.literal: only Sizhou, because of past attack and defense, has enmity already deep; it should be reorganized, so that both sides may benefit."
translations.idiomatic: only Sizhou, scarred by years of siege and counter-siege, should be reorganized so both sides gain."

sentences.zh: 詔從之，徐州依舊爲觀察使，統徐、濠、宿三州，泗州爲團練使，割隸淮南。

translations.literal: An edict followed their advice: Xuzhou remained an observation commission, governing Xu, Hao, and Su; Sizhou became a training commission and was cut off to be placed under Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed: Xuzhou kept its observation commission over Xu, Hao, and Su; Sizhou became a training commission under Huainan.

sentences.zh: 加幽州節度使張允伸兼侍中。

translations.literal: Youzhou Military Commissioner Zhang Yunshen was additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yunshen, commissioner of Youzhou, was also made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，乙未，同昌公主薨。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on yiwei, Princess Tongchang died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on yiwei, Princess Tongchang died.

sentences.zh: 上痛悼不已，殺翰林醫官韓宗劭等二十-{餘}-人，悉收捕其親族三百-{餘}-人-{系}-京兆獄。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved without end, executed more than twenty Hanlin medical officers including Han Zongshao, and arrested all their kin—more than three hundred people—and imprisoned them in the Jingzhao jail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was inconsolable. He executed more than twenty Hanlin physicians, including Han Zongshao, and threw more than three hundred of their relatives into the Jingzhao jail.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同平章事劉瞻召諫官使言之，諫官莫敢言者，乃自上言，以爲：「修短之期，人之定分。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor Liu Zhan summoned remonstrance officials to speak; none dared speak, so he himself submitted a memorial, stating: "The span of life long or short is man's allotted portion.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director and Grand Councillor Liu Zhan called on the remonstrance officials to speak up; none dared, so he memorialized in his own name: "Long life and short are each man's allotted share.

sentences.zh: 昨公主有疾，深軫聖慈。

translations.literal: When the princess fell ill yesterday, Your Majesty's compassion was deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess fell ill, Your Majesty's grief was profound.

sentences.zh: 宗劭等診療之時，惟求疾愈，備施方-{術}-，非不盡心，而禍福難移，竟成差跌，原其情狀，亦可哀矜。

translations.literal: When Zongshao and the others treated her, they sought only that the illness be cured and applied every remedy and technique—they were not without diligence—but fortune and misfortune cannot be shifted, and in the end it came to failure; considering their circumstances, they too deserve pity.
translations.idiomatic: Zongshao and his colleagues sought only her recovery and tried every remedy—they were not negligent—but fate cannot be bargained with, and in the end she died. Their plight deserves pity.

sentences.zh: 而械-{系}-老幼三百-{餘}-人，物議沸騰。

translations.literal: Yet more than three hundred old and young were shackled and imprisoned, and public opinion seethed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet more than three hundred of their kin, old and young, sit in chains, and public outrage is boiling over.

sentences.zh: 道路嗟歎。

translations.literal: On the roads people sighed in lament.
translations.idiomatic: People on the roads sigh in dismay.

sentences.zh: 奈何以達理知命之君，渉肆暴不明之謗！

translations.literal: How can a ruler who understands principle and accepts fate involve himself in the reproach of wanton violence and lack of clarity!
translations.idiomatic: How can a ruler who knows fate and reason invite the charge of arbitrary cruelty!

sentences.zh: 蓋由安不慮危，忿不思難之故也。

translations.literal: This is surely because, in security one does not consider danger, and in anger one does not think of difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: This comes of resting in security without heeding danger, and giving way to anger without weighing the cost.

sentences.zh: 伏-{願}-少回聖慮，寬釋-{系}-者。」

translations.literal: I humbly beg that Your Sacred Majesty turn your consideration slightly and release those who are imprisoned."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that Your Majesty reconsider slightly and release the prisoners."

sentences.zh: 上覽疎，不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and took offense.

sentences.zh: 瞻又與京兆尹温璋力諫-{於}-上前，上大怒，叱出之。

translations.literal: Zhan again, together with Metropolitan Governor Wen Zhang, remonstrated strenuously before the emperor; the emperor flew into a rage and shouted them out.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan and Metropolitan Governor Wen Zhang pressed their remonstrance before the throne; the emperor flew into a rage and had them driven out.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使何全皞年少，驕暴好殺，又減將士衣糧。

translations.literal: He Quanhao, military commissioner of Weibo, was young, arrogant and brutal, fond of killing, and also reduced the soldiers' rations and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: He Quanhao, commissioner of Weibo, was young, proud, violent, and bloodthirsty, and he had cut the troops' pay and rations.

sentences.zh: 將士作亂，全皞單騎走，追殺之，推大將韓君雄爲留-{後}-。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers mutinied; Quanhao fled alone on horseback, was pursued and killed, and they elevated General Han Junxiong as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The troops mutinied. Quanhao fled alone on horseback; they ran him down and killed him, then set up the general Han Junxiong as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 成德節度使王景崇爲之請旌節。

translations.literal: Wang Jingchong, military commissioner of Chengde, requested the imperial commission for him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingchong of Chengde petitioned the court for an imperial commission on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚戌，以君雄爲魏博留-{後}-。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on gengxu, Junxiong was appointed acting commissioner of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengxu, Han Junxiong was made acting commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以劉瞻同平章事，充荊南節度使。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Liu Zhan, Associate Grand Councillor, was appointed military commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Liu Zhan was removed from court and sent out as military commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 貶温璋振州司馬。

translations.literal: Wen Zhang was demoted to secretary of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhang was demoted to regimental aide of Zhen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 璋歎曰：「生不逢時，死何足惜！」

translations.literal: Zhang sighed and said: "Born in the wrong age—what is death to regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhang sighed: "To live in such times—why should death matter?"

sentences.zh: 是夕，仰藥卒。

translations.literal: That evening he took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: That night he swallowed poison and died.

sentences.zh: 庚申，敕曰：「苟無蠹害，何至-{於}-斯！

translations.literal: On gengshen an edict said: "If he had not been a pest, how could it have come to this!
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen an edict declared: "Had he not been a menace, how could it have come to this!

sentences.zh: 惡實貫盈，死有-{餘}-責。

translations.literal: His wickedness was full to overflowing; even in death his guilt remained.
translations.idiomatic: His crimes overflowed the measure—death left him still in debt to justice.

sentences.zh: 宜令三日内且-{於}-城外權瘞，俟經恩宥，方許歸葬，使中外快心，-{奸}-邪知懼。」

translations.literal: He should be provisionally buried outside the city within three days; only after receiving imperial grace may burial in his home region be permitted, so that within and without the court may rejoice and the wicked and depraved may know fear."
translations.idiomatic: Within three days bury him provisionally outside the walls; only after an act of grace may his kin reclaim the body for proper burial—so court and country may take satisfaction and the wicked may learn fear."

sentences.zh: 己巳，貶右諫議大夫髙湘、比部郎中知-{制}-誥楊知至、禮部郎中魏簹等-{於}-嶺南，皆坐與劉瞻親善，爲韋保衡所逐也。

translations.literal: On jisi, Right Remonstrance Grandee Gao Xiang, Director of the Bureau of Review and Drafter of Imperial Edicts Yang Zhizhi, Ministry of Rites Bureau Director Wei Dang, and others were demoted to Lingnan—all for being close to Liu Zhan and driven out by Wei Baoheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the court banished Right Remonstrance Grandee Gao Xiang, Yang Zhizhi of the Bureau of Review and Edicts, Wei Dang of the Ministry of Rites, and others to Lingnan—all friends of Liu Zhan, purged by Wei Baoheng.

sentences.zh: 知至，汝士之子；

translations.literal: Zhizhi was the son of Rushi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhizhi was the son of Yang Rushi.

sentences.zh: 簹，扶之子也。

translations.literal: Dang was Fu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dang was the son of Wei Fu.

sentences.zh: 保衡又與路巖共譖劉瞻，去與醫官通謀，誤投毒藥。

translations.literal: Baoheng also joined with Lu Yan in slandering Liu Zhan, alleging that he had conspired with a medical officer and mistakenly administered poison.
translations.idiomatic: Baoheng and Lu Yan also smeared Liu Zhan, claiming he had colluded with a palace physician and accidentally given poison.

sentences.zh: 丙子，貶瞻康州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Zhan was demoted to prefect of Kangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Liu Zhan was demoted to prefect of Kang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士承旨鄭畋草瞻罷相-{制}-辭曰：「安數畝之居，仍非己有；

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician-in-Charge Zheng Tian drafted the edict removing Zhan from the chancellorship, which read: "Content with a dwelling of a few acres, yet even that was not his own;
translations.idiomatic: Chief Hanlin Academician Zheng Tian drafted the edict dismissing Liu Zhan: "He could be content with a cottage on a few acres, yet even that he did not truly own;

sentences.zh: 卻四方之賂，惟畏人知。」

translations.literal: he refused bribes from all quarters, fearing only that men would know."
translations.idiomatic: he turned back gifts from every quarter, dreading only discovery."

sentences.zh: 巖謂畋曰：「侍郎乃表-{薦}-劉相也！」

translations.literal: Yan said to Tian: "The Vice Director was the one who recommended Chancellor Liu in the first place!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yan told Zheng Tian: "You were the one who put Liu Zhan forward!"

sentences.zh: 坐貶梧州刺史。

translations.literal: For this he was demoted to prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For this Zheng Tian was demoted to prefect of Wu prefecture.

sentences.zh: -{御}-史中丞孫瑝坐爲瞻所擢用，亦貶汀州刺史。

translations.literal: Sun Huang, Vice Censor-in-Chief, was demoted to prefect of Tingzhou for having been promoted by Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Huang, the vice censor-in-chief, had been raised by Liu Zhan and was likewise banished to Ting prefecture.

sentences.zh: 路巖素與劉瞻論議多不-{葉}-，瞻既貶康州，巖猶不快，閲《十道圖》，以歡州去長安萬-{里}-，再貶歡州司戸。

translations.literal: Lu Yan had long differed with Liu Zhan in debate; though Zhan had already been demoted to Kangzhou, Yan was still unsatisfied. Consulting the Ten Circuits Atlas, he found that Huanzhou was ten thousand li from Chang'an, and had Zhan demoted again to registrar of Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yan had never seen eye to eye with Liu Zhan. Even after Liu was sent to Kangzhou, Yan was not satisfied; checking the Ten Circuits Atlas and noting that Huanzhou lay ten thousand li from Chang'an, he had Liu demoted again—to registrar of Huan.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸卯，以西川留-{後}-呉行魯爲節度使。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on guimao, Wu Xinglu, acting commissioner of Western Shu, was appointed military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on guimao, Wu Xinglu was confirmed as military commissioner of Western Shu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛亥，以兵部尚書、鹽鐵轉運使王鐸爲禮部尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinhai, Minister of War and Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner Wang Duo was appointed Minister of Rites and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinhai, Wang Duo, minister of war and salt commissioner, was made minister of rites and grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 鐸起之兄子也。

translations.literal: Duo was the nephew of Wang Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo was a nephew of Wang Qi.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，-{復}-以徐州爲感化軍節度。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Xuzhou was again made the seat of the Ganhua Army command.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Xuzhou was again named seat of the Ganhua command.

sentences.zh: 十二月，加成德節度使王景崇同平章事，以左金吾上將軍李國昌爲振武節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Wang Jingchong, military commissioner of Chengde, was given the additional title Associate Grand Councillor, and Left Golden Guard General Li Guochang was appointed military commissioner of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Wang Jingchong of Chengde was made associate grand councillor, and Li Guochang, senior general of the Left Golden Guard, was named commissioner of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛酉，葬文懿公主。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinyou, Princess Wenyì was buried.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on xinyou, Princess Wenyì was laid to rest.

sentences.zh: 韋氏之人爭取庭祭之灰，汰其金銀。

translations.literal: People of the Wei clan scrambled for the ashes of the courtyard offerings, sifting out the gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Members of the Wei clan fought over the ashes of the funeral offerings, panning them for gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 凡服玩，毎物皆百二十輿，以錦繡、珠玉爲儀衞、明器，輝煥二十-{餘}--{里}-。

translations.literal: For all clothing and playthings, each item required one hundred twenty cartloads; imperial guards and grave goods of brocade, pearls, and jade blazed in splendor for more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: Every article of clothing and treasure went out in trains of a hundred and twenty carts; funeral guards and grave goods in brocade, pearls, and jade made a blaze of color for twenty li.

sentences.zh: 賜酒百斛、餅食炎四十橐駝，以飼體夫。

translations.literal: A hundred hu of wine and forty camel-loads of baked cakes were granted to feed the cart bearers.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispensed a hundred hu of wine and forty camels' loads of warm cakes for the carriers.

sentences.zh: 上與郭淑妃思公主不已，樂工李可及作《歎百年-{曲}-》，其聲心妻惋，舞者數百人，-{發}-内庫雜寶爲其首飾，以絁八百匹爲地衣，舞罷，珠璣覆地。

translations.literal: The emperor and Consort Guo Shu could not cease grieving for the princess. Musician Li Keji composed the "Song of Lament for a Century"; its melody was heart-wrenchingly mournful. Several hundred dancers wore ornaments fashioned from miscellaneous treasures of the inner treasury; eight hundred bolts of silk served as a ground cloth, and when the dance ended pearls and gems covered the floor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong and Consort Guo mourned the princess without end. Court musician Li Keji composed "Lament for a Hundred Years," its air heartbreakingly sad. Several hundred dancers wore ornaments hammered from the inner treasury's jewels; eight hundred bolts of coarse silk carpeted the floor, and when the dance ended pearls and gems lay scattered everywhere.

sentences.zh: 以魏博留-{後}-韓君雄爲節度使。

translations.literal: Han Junxiong, acting commissioner of Weibo, was appointed military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Han Junxiong was confirmed as military commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎、同平章事路巖與韋保衡素相表裡，勢傾天下。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Grand Councillor Lu Yan and Wei Baoheng had long been inside and outside to each other; their power tilted the world.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yan, vice director and grand councillor, and Wei Baoheng had long been partners in power, and together they dominated the empire.

sentences.zh: 既而爭權，浸有隙，保衡遂短巖-{於}-上。

translations.literal: Before long they contested power, and rifts gradually appeared; Baoheng then spoke ill of Yan to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They soon fell out over power; Baoheng began whispering against Lu Yan at court.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸卯，以巖同平章事，充西川節度使。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guimao, Yan, Associate Grand Councillor, was appointed military commissioner of Western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on guimao, Lu Yan was sent out as military commissioner of Western Shu.

sentences.zh: 巖出城，路人以瓦礫擲之。

translations.literal: As Yan left the city, passersby pelted him with tiles and stones.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Yan left the capital, people hurled tiles and stones at him.

sentences.zh: 權京兆尹薛能，巖所擢也，巖謂能曰：「臨行，煩以瓦礫相餞！」

translations.literal: Acting Metropolitan Governor Xue Neng, whom Yan had promoted—Yan said to Neng: "On my departure you honor me with a farewell of tiles and stones!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yan said to Xue Neng, the acting metropolitan governor whom he had raised: "A fine send-off—tiles and stones as my parting gift!"

sentences.zh: 能徐舉笏對曰：「向來宰相出，府司無例-{發}-人防衞。」

translations.literal: Neng slowly raised his tablet and replied: "When chancellors have left in the past, this office has had no precedent of dispatching men for protection."
translations.idiomatic: Xue Neng slowly raised his court tablet: "When past chancellors departed, this office never posted guards—it had no precedent."

sentences.zh: 巖甚慚。

translations.literal: Yan was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yan was thoroughly humiliated.

sentences.zh: 能，汾州人也。

translations.literal: Neng was a native of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Neng was from Fen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五月，上幸安國寺，贈僧重謙、僧澈沉檀講座二，各髙二丈。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the emperor visited Anguo Temple and bestowed on the monks Chongqian and Che two agarwood lecture seats, each two zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor visited Anguo Temple and gave the monks Chongqian and Che two lecture thrones of agarwood, each twenty feet high.

sentences.zh: 設萬人齋。

translations.literal: A ten-thousand-person vegetarian feast was arranged.
translations.idiomatic: The court held a feast for ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以兵部尚書盧耽同平章事，充山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Minister of War Lu Dan was appointed Associate Grand Councillor and military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Lu Dan was made grand councillor and military commissioner of Shannan East.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，以兵部侍郎、鹽鐵轉運使劉鄴爲禮部尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Vice Minister of War and Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner Liu Ye was appointed Minister of Rites and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Liu Ye, vice minister of war and salt commissioner, was made minister of rites and grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，幽州節度使張允伸得風疾，請委軍政就醫。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Zhang Yunshen, military commissioner of Youzhou, contracted wind disease and requested to entrust military and civil affairs so he could seek medical treatment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring Zhang Yunshen of Youzhou fell ill with paralysis and asked leave to hand over command and seek treatment.

sentences.zh: 許之，以其子簡會爲留-{後}-。

translations.literal: Permission was granted, and his son Jianhui was made acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed and named his son Jianhui acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 疾甚，遣使上表納旌節。

translations.literal: When the illness grew severe, he sent envoys to submit a memorial surrendering his commission.
translations.idiomatic: As he worsened he sent in his commission by memorial.

sentences.zh: 丙申，薨。

translations.literal: On bingshen he died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen he died.

sentences.zh: 允伸鎭幽州二十三年，勤儉恭謹，邊鄙無警，上下安之。

translations.literal: Yunshen had governed Youzhou for twenty-three years, industrious and frugal, respectful and careful; the frontier knew no alarm, and superiors and subordinates alike were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty-three years Zhang Yunshen had held Youzhou—thrifty, diligent, and decorous—and the border had been quiet; high and low were content.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁巳，以兵部侍郎、同平章事-{-{于}-}-琮爲山南東道節度使，以刑部侍郎、判戸部奉天趙隱爲戸部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the second month, on dingsi, Vice Minister of War and Associate Grand Councillor Yu Cong was appointed military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, and Vice Minister of Justice and Acting Director of the Ministry of Revenue Zhao Yin of Fengtian was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingsi, Yu Cong was sent to Shannan East as military commissioner, and Zhao Yin of Fengtian, vice minister of justice and acting head of revenue, was made vice minister of revenue and grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 平州刺史張公素，素有威望，爲幽人所服。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongsu, prefect of Pingzhou, had long enjoyed prestige and was respected by the people of You.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongsu, prefect of Ping, had long stood high in esteem and commanded the respect of the Youzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 張允伸薨，公素帥州兵來奔喪。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yunshen died, Gongsu led his prefectural troops to come attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yunshen died, Gongsu marched his prefectural troops to the funeral.

sentences.zh: 張簡會懼，三月，奔京師，以爲諸衞將軍。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianhui was afraid; in the third month he fled to the capital and was made a general of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Jianhui, unnerved, fled to the capital in the third month and was given a post as palace guard general.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，立皇子保爲吉王，傑爲壽王，倚爲睦王。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the prince Bao was enfeoffed as Prince of Ji, Jie as Prince of Shou, and Yi as Prince of Mu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Prince Bao was named Prince of Ji, Jie Prince of Shou, and Yi Prince of Mu.

sentences.zh: 以張公素爲平盧留-{後}-。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongsu was appointed acting commissioner of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongsu was made acting commissioner of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 五月，國子司業韋殷裕詣閣門告郭淑妃弟内作坊使敬述陰事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Guozi Vice Director Wei Yinyu went to the Gate of Audience to accuse Jingshu, commissioner of the Inner Workshop and younger brother of Consort Guo Shu, of secret wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Wei Yinyu, vice director of the Directorate of Education, appeared at the Gate of Audience to denounce Jingshu—the consort's brother and head of the inner workshops—for covert misconduct.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，杖殺殷裕，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious; Yinyu was beaten to death and his household confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, had Wei Yinyu beaten to death, and seized his property.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，閣門使田獻銛奪紫，改橋陵使，以其受殷裕狀故也。

translations.literal: On yihai, Gate of Audience Commissioner Tian Xianqian was stripped of his purple robe and reassigned as commissioner of Qiao Mausoleum, because he had accepted Yinyu's petition.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Tian Xianqian lost his purple robe and was demoted to warden of Qiao Mausoleum for having accepted Wei Yinyu's petition.

sentences.zh: 殷裕妻父太府少卿崔元應、妻從兄中書-{舍}-人崔沆、季父君卿皆貶嶺南官；

translations.literal: Yinyu's father-in-law, Vice Director of the Grand Storehouse Cui Yuanying; his wife's older cousin, Drafting Office Attendant Cui Hang; and his uncle Junqing were all demoted to posts in Lingnan;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanying, vice director of the grand storehouse and Wei Yinyu's father-in-law; Cui Hang, drafting attendant and the wife's cousin; and the uncle Cui Junqing were all banished to posts in Lingnan;

sentences.zh: 給事中杜裔休坐與殷裕善，亦貶端州司戸。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Du Yixiu, for being friendly with Yinyu, was also demoted to registrar of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yixiu, a supervising secretary and Wei Yinyu's friend, was sent down to registrar of Duan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 沆，鉉之子也。

translations.literal: Hang was the son of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hang was the son of Cui Xuan.

sentences.zh: 裔休，悰之子也。

translations.literal: Yixiu was Cong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yixiu was the son of Du Cong.

sentences.zh: 丙子，貶山南東道節度使-{-{于}-}-琮爲普王傅、分司，韋保衡譖之也。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Yu Cong, military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, was demoted to tutor of the Prince of Pu and assigned to the detached service bureau, because Wei Baoheng had slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Yu Cong was stripped of Shannan East and reduced to tutor of the Prince of Pu in nominal office—all on Wei Baoheng's word.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，貶尚書左承李當、吏部侍郎王渢、左散騎常侍李都、翰林學士承旨兵部侍郎張楊、前中書-{舍}-人封彦卿、左諫議大夫楊塾；

translations.literal: On xinsi, Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat Li Dang, Vice Minister of the Civil Office Wang Fu, Left Regular Attendant Li Du, Hanlin Academician-in-Charge and Vice Minister of War Zhang Yang, former Drafting Office Attendant Feng Yanqing, and Left Remonstrance Grandee Yang Shu were demoted;
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Li Dang, left assistant minister; Wang Fu, vice minister of the civil office; Li Du, left attendant; chief Hanlin Zhang Yang; former drafting attendant Feng Yanqing; and Yang Shu, left remonstrance grandee—all were banished;

sentences.zh: 癸未，貶工部尚書嚴祁、給事中李貺、給事中張鐸、左金吾大將軍李敬仲、起居-{舍}-人蕭遘、李瀆、鄭彦特、李藻，皆處之湖、嶺之南，坐與琮厚善故也，貺，漢之子；

translations.literal: On guiwei, Minister of Works Yan Qi, Supervising Secretaries Li Kuang and Zhang Duo, Left Golden Guard General Li Jingzhong, Diarists Xiao You, Li Du, Zheng Yante, and Li Zao were all banished south of the lakes and Ling ranges—for being close friends of Yu Cong; Kuang was Han's son;
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Yan Qi, minister of works; Li Kuang and Zhang Duo, supervising secretaries; Li Jingzhong, Left Golden Guard general; and diarists Xiao You, Li Du, Zheng Yante, and Li Zao—all were sent south of the lakes and mountains for their ties to Yu Cong. Li Kuang was the son of Li Han;

sentences.zh: 遘，置之子也。

translations.literal: You was Zhi's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao You was the son of Xiao Zhi.

sentences.zh: 甲申，貶前平盧節度使-{於}-琄爲涼王府長史、分司，前湖南觀察使-{於}-瑰袁州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiashen, former military commissioner of Pinglu Yu Juan was demoted to chief secretary of the Prince of Liang's establishment and assigned to detached service, and former Hunan Observation Commissioner Yu Gui was made prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Yu Juan, former commissioner of Pinglu, was reduced to chief secretary to the Prince of Liang in nominal service, and Yu Gui, former Hunan observer, to prefect of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 瑰、琄，皆琮之兄也。

translations.literal: Gui and Juan were both elder brothers of Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gui and Yu Juan were Yu Cong's elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 尋再貶琮韶州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long Cong was demoted again to prefect of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yu Cong was demoted again—to prefect of Shao.

sentences.zh: 琮妻廣德公主，上之妹也，與琮皆之韶州，行則肩輿門相對，坐則執琮之帶，琮由是獲全。

translations.literal: Cong's wife was Princess Guangde, the emperor's younger sister; she went with Cong to Shaozhou, and when they traveled their shoulder-palanquins faced each other gate to gate; when seated she held Cong's belt—thus Cong was preserved safe.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Cong's wife was Princess Guangde, the emperor's sister. She accompanied him to Shao; on the road their palanquins traveled facing each other, and when seated she held his belt—by this Yu Cong survived.

sentences.zh: 時諸公主多驕縱，惟廣德動遵法度，事-{于}-氏宗親尊卑無不如禮，内外稱之。

translations.literal: At the time most princesses were arrogant and unrestrained; only Guangde consistently observed the law, treating Yu-clan relatives high and low without failing in propriety, and was praised within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Most princesses of the day were haughty and overbearing; Guangde alone adhered to decorum in all dealings with the Yu kindred, high or low, and won praise throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 六月，以盧龍留-{後}-張公素爲節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Zhang Gongsu, acting commissioner of Lulong, was appointed military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zhang Gongsu was confirmed as military commissioner of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 韋保衡欲以其黨裴條爲郎官，憚左丞李璋方嚴，恐其不放上，先遣人達意。

translations.literal: Wei Baoheng wished to install his follower Pei Tiao as a palace secretary but feared Left Assistant Minister Li Zhang, who was stern, lest he refuse to pass the appointment upward; he first sent someone to convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Baoheng wanted his man Pei Tiao made a palace secretary but feared the upright Li Zhang would block the appointment, and sent an emissary ahead to sound him out.

sentences.zh: 璋曰：「朝廷遷除，不應見問。」

translations.literal: Zhang said: "Court appointments and removals should not be subject to private inquiry."
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhang replied: "Imperial appointments are not matters for private negotiation."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙未，以璋爲宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on yiwei, Zhang was appointed observation commissioner of Xuanzhou and Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on yiwei, Li Zhang was sent out as observer of Xuan and She.

sentences.zh: 八月，歸義節度使張義潮薨，沙州長史曹義金代領軍府。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Zhang Yichao, military commissioner of Guiyi, died; Cao Yijin, prefectural secretary of Shazhou, took over the military headquarters in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zhang Yichao of Guiyi died; Cao Yijin, chief secretary of Shazhou, assumed command of the circuit.

sentences.zh: -{制}-以義金爲歸義節度使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yijin military commissioner of Guiyi.
translations.idiomatic: By edict Cao Yijin was named commissioner of Guiyi.

sentences.zh: 是-{後}-中原多故，朝命不及，回鶻陷甘州，自-{餘}-諸州録歸義者多爲羌、胡所據。

translations.literal: After this the Central Plains saw many troubles, and imperial orders could not reach in time; the Uyghurs captured Ganzhou, and of the remaining prefectures nominally under Guiyi most were seized by Qiang and Hu peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter turmoil in the heartland kept imperial writ from reaching the west; the Uyghurs took Ganzhou, and most of the other prefectures still enrolled under Guiyi fell to Qiang and Hu powers.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，追上宣宗謚曰元聖至明成武獻文睿智章仁神聰懿道大孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, posthumous honors were conferred on Emperor Xuanzong: Emperor of Original Sagacity, Supreme Brightness, Accomplished Martiality, Dedicated Culture, Profound Wisdom, Manifest Benevolence, Divine Intelligence, Virtuous Way, and Great Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter the court added the posthumous title for the late Emperor Xuanzong: "Original Sage, Supreme Bright, Accomplished in War, Devoted in Letters, Profound in Wisdom, Manifest in Benevolence, Spiritually Perceptive, Virtuous in the Way, Great in Filial Piety."

sentences.zh: 振武節度使李國昌，恃功恣橫，專殺長吏。

translations.literal: Li Guochang, military commissioner of Zhenwu, relied on his merits, acted wantonly and overbearing, and on his own authority killed senior officials.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guochang of Zhenwu, bloated by his service record, ran wild and executed senior officers at will.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不能平，徙國昌爲大同軍防-{禦}-使，國昌稱疾不赴。

translations.literal: The court could not restrain him and transferred Guochang to be defense commissioner of Datong Army; Guochang claimed illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to curb him, the court transferred Li Guochang to the Datong defense command; he pleaded illness and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，癸巳，上遣敕使詣法門寺迎佛骨，群臣諫者甚衆，至有言憲宗迎佛骨尋晏駕者。

translations.literal: In spring, the third month, on guisi, the emperor dispatched an imperial envoy to Famen Temple to welcome the Buddha's relic; many among the ministers remonstrated, some even saying that when Emperor Xianzong welcomed the Buddha's relic he soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of spring, on guisi, the emperor sent an envoy to Famen Temple to fetch the Buddha's bone. Many ministers protested; some reminded him that Emperor Xianzong had died soon after welcoming the relic.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕生得見之，死亦無恨！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If in life I can see it, in death I shall have no regret!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "To see it in life would leave me nothing to regret in death!"

sentences.zh: 廣造浮圖、寶帳、香輿、幡花、幢蓋以迎之，皆飾以金玉、錦繡、珠翠。

translations.literal: He had pagodas, treasure pavilions, incense chariots, banner flowers, and canopied banners built on a grand scale to welcome it, all adorned with gold, jade, brocade, pearls, and kingfisher feathers.
translations.idiomatic: The court built pagodas, jeweled pavilions, incense palanquins, banners, flowers, and canopies to meet it—every piece trimmed in gold, jade, brocade, pearls, and kingfisher plumes.

sentences.zh: 自京城至寺三百-{里}-間，道路車馬，晝夜不絶。

translations.literal: From the capital to the temple, over three hundred li, carts and horses on the roads did not cease day or night.
translations.idiomatic: For three hundred li from the capital to the temple the roads teemed with traffic night and day.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬寅，佛骨至京師，導以禁軍兵仗、公私音樂，沸天燭地，綿亙數十-{里}-。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renyin, the Buddha's relic reached the capital; it was led in with palace guard arms and public and private music, boiling heaven and lighting earth, stretching continuously for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on renyin, the relic reached the capital under palace guard escort and a din of official and private music that shook heaven and lit the earth for dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 儀衞之盛，過-{於}-郊祀，元和之時不及遠矣。

translations.literal: The splendor of the ceremonial guard exceeded that of the suburban sacrifices; the Yuanhe era fell far short by comparison.
translations.idiomatic: The procession outshone a suburban sacrifice; nothing in the Yuanhe reign had come close.

sentences.zh: 富室夾道爲彩樓及無遮會，競爲侈靡。

translations.literal: Wealthy households lined the road with colored towers and "Unhindered" assemblies, competing in extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: The rich built festival towers and open alms halls along the route, vying in lavish display.

sentences.zh: 上-{御}-安福門，降樓膜拜，流涕沾臆，賜僧及京城耆老嘗見元和事者金帛。

translations.literal: The emperor attended at Anfu Gate, descended the tower to prostrate himself in worship, tears soaking his chest; he bestowed gold and silk on monks and aged residents of the capital who had witnessed events of the Yuanhe era.
translations.idiomatic: At Anfu Gate the emperor descended to kneel and worship, weeping until his breast was wet; he gave gold and cloth to monks and to elders who remembered the Yuanhe years.

sentences.zh: 迎佛骨入禁中，三日，出置安國崇化寺。

translations.literal: The Buddha's relic was welcomed into the Forbidden City; after three days it was taken out and placed at Anguo Chonghua Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The relic was brought into the palace, kept three days, then moved to Anguo Chonghua Temple.

sentences.zh: 宰相已下競施金帛，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: From the chancellors downward all competed in presenting gold and silk beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: From the chancellor down, officials showered gifts of gold and silk beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 因下德音，降中外-{系}-囚。

translations.literal: Thereupon a grace edict was issued, commuting prisoners within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed with a general amnesty, releasing prisoners at court and across the empire.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁亥，以西川節度使路巖兼中書令。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dinghai, Lu Yan, military commissioner of Western Shu, was additionally appointed Grand Secretary of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dinghai, Lu Yan of Western Shu was made grand secretary of the Secretariat as well.

sentences.zh: 南詔寇西川，又寇黔南，黔中經略使秦匡謀兵少不敵，棄城奔荊南。

translations.literal: Nanzhao raided Western Shu and also raided Qiannan; Qin Kuangmou, military commissioner of Qianzhong, had too few troops to resist, abandoned his city, and fled to Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao struck Western Shu and then Qiannan; Qin Kuangmou of Qianzhong, outnumbered, abandoned his post and fled toward Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 荊南節度使杜悰囚而奏之。

translations.literal: Du Cong, military commissioner of Jingnan, imprisoned him and reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong of Jingnan seized him, held him prisoner, and memorialized the throne.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙未，敕斬匡謀，籍沒其家貲，親族應縁坐者，令有司搜捕以聞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day yiwei, an edict ordered Kuangmou beheaded; his family's property was confiscated, and kinsmen liable for collective punishment were to be searched out and arrested by the relevant offices, with reports submitted to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the yiwei day, an edict commanded the execution of Kuangmou and the confiscation of his family's wealth. Relatives subject to guilt by association were to be hunted down by the proper authorities and reported to the court.

sentences.zh: 匡謀，鳳翔人也。

translations.literal: Kuangmou was a native of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangmou was from Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 以中書侍郎、同平章事王鐸同平章事，充宣武節度使。

translations.literal: Wang Duo, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Councillor, was appointed Concurrent Grand Councillor and Military Commissioner of Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo, vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent grand councillor, was confirmed as grand councillor and named military commissioner of Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 時韋保衡挾恩弄權，以劉瞻、-{-{于}-}-琮先在相位，不禮-{於}-己，譖而逐之。

translations.literal: At this time Wei Baoheng, relying on imperial favor, wielded power arbitrarily. Because Liu Zhan and Yu Cong had held the chief ministership before him and had not shown him due respect, he slandered them and had them driven from office.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Baoheng was then trading on imperial favor to wield power as he pleased. Liu Zhan and Yu Cong had served as chief ministers before him and had not treated him with proper deference, so he slandered them and drove them from court.

sentences.zh: 王鐸，保衡及第時主文也，蕭遘，同年進士也，二人素薄保衡之爲人，保衡皆擯斥之。

translations.literal: Wang Duo had been chief examiner when Baoheng passed the examinations; Xiao You was a fellow successful candidate of the same year. Both men had long looked down on Baoheng's character, and Baoheng in turn ostracized them both.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo had presided over the examinations when Baoheng earned his degree; Xiao You had passed in the same year. Both had always held Baoheng's character in low regard, and Baoheng had them both pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊寅，上疾大漸，左軍中尉劉行深、右軍中尉韓文約立少子普王儼。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day wuyin, as the emperor's illness reached its crisis, Left Army Commandant Liu Xingshen and Right Army Commandant Han Wenyue installed his youngest son, Prince Pu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the wuyin day, as the emperor's illness worsened sharply, Left Army Commandant Liu Xingshen and Right Army Commandant Han Wenyue put the youngest son, Prince Pu Yi, on the throne.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，-{制}-：「立儼爲皇太子，權句當軍國政事。」

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, an edict proclaimed: "Prince Yi is established as crown prince and is to handle military and state affairs provisionally."
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day, an edict declared: "Prince Yi is hereby named crown prince and shall provisionally manage military and state affairs."

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, the emperor died in the Hall of Tranquil Blessing.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day, the emperor died in the Hall of Tranquil Blessing.

sentences.zh: 遺詔書韋保衡攝塚宰。

translations.literal: The testamentary edict appointed Wei Baoheng acting chief mourner for the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: The deathbed edict named Wei Baoheng to serve as acting chief mourner.

sentences.zh: 僖宗即位。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁未，追尊母王貴妃爲皇太-{后}-，劉行深、韓文約皆封國公。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day dingwei, the emperor's mother, Imperial Consort Wang, was posthumously honored as empress dowager; Liu Xingshen and Han Wenyue were both enfeoffed as dukes of a state.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the dingwei day, his mother, Lady Wang, was posthumously elevated to empress dowager, and both Liu Xingshen and Han Wenyue were made dukes.

sentences.zh: 關東、河南大水。

translations.literal: Great floods struck east of the Pass and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Catastrophic floods ravaged the region east of the Pass and Henan.

sentences.zh: 九月，有司上先太-{后}-謚曰惠安。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the relevant offices submitted the posthumous title Huian for the late empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the proper offices proposed the posthumous title Huian—"Benevolent and Tranquil"—for the late empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 司徒、門下侍郎、同平章事韋保衡，怨家告其陰事，貶保衡賀州刺史。

translations.literal: Wei Baoheng, Minister of Education, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Concurrent Grand Councillor, was denounced by an enemy for secret misdeeds and demoted to prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: An enemy denounced Wei Baoheng—minister of education, vice director of the chancellery, and grand councillor—for hidden misconduct, and he was demoted to prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 樂工李可及流嶺南。

translations.literal: The musician Li Keji was banished to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The musician Li Keji was exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 可及有寵-{於}-懿宗，嘗爲子娶婦，懿宗賜之酒二銀壺，啓之無酒而中實。

translations.literal: Keji enjoyed Emperor Yizong's favor. When he arranged a marriage for his son, Yizong bestowed on him two silver flasks of wine; when opened, they held no wine but were filled with solid things instead.
translations.idiomatic: Keji had won Emperor Yizong's favor. When he married off his son, the emperor gave him two silver wine jars—but they contained no wine, only something solid inside.

sentences.zh: 右軍中尉西門季玄屢以爲言，懿宗不-{聽}-。

translations.literal: Right Army Commandant Ximen Jixuan spoke of this repeatedly, but Yizong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Right Army Commandant Ximen Jixuan complained about this again and again, but Yizong paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 可及嘗大受賜物，載以官車。

translations.literal: Keji once received a great quantity of gifts and transported them in official carts.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion Keji received a lavish bounty of gifts and had them hauled away in government wagons.

sentences.zh: 季玄謂曰：「汝它日破家，此物-{復}-應以官車載還。

translations.literal: Jixuan said to him: "When you ruin your family one day, these things ought again to be carried back in official carts.
translations.idiomatic: Jixuan told him, "The day you lose everything, those same goods will have to be hauled back in official wagons.

sentences.zh: 非爲受賜，徒煩牛足耳！」

translations.literal: It is not for receiving gifts—it is only to weary the oxen's hooves in vain!"
translations.idiomatic: This isn't about receiving gifts—it's just wasting the oxen's legs for nothing!"

sentences.zh: 及流嶺南，籍沒其家，果如季玄言。

translations.literal: When he was banished to Lingnan and his family's property was confiscated, it proved exactly as Jixuan had said.
translations.idiomatic: When he was exiled to Lingnan and his estate was confiscated, events unfolded exactly as Jixuan had predicted.

sentences.zh: 以西川節度使路巖兼侍中，加成德節度使王景崇中書令，魏博節度使韓君雄、盧龍節度使張公素、天平節度使髙駢-{並}-同平章事。

translations.literal: The Sichuan military commissioner Lu Yan was additionally made Palace Secretary; Chengde military commissioner Wang Jingchong was made Director of the Secretariat; Weibo military commissioner Han Junxiong, Lulong military commissioner Zhang Gongsu, and Tianping military commissioner Gao Pian were all made Concurrent Grand Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yan, military commissioner of Sichuan, was also made palace secretary; Wang Jingchong of Chengde was promoted to director of the Secretariat; and Han Junxiong of Weibo, Zhang Gongsu of Lulong, and Gao Pian of Tianping were all appointed concurrent grand councillors.

sentences.zh: 君雄仍賜名允中。

translations.literal: Junxiong was further granted the name Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Junxiong was also granted the name Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙未，以左-{僕}-射蕭倣爲門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day yiwei, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Xiao Fang was made Vice Director of the Chancellery and Concurrent Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the yiwei day, Xiao Fang, left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed vice director of the chancellery and grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 韋保衡再貶崖州澄邁令，尋賜自盡；

translations.literal: Wei Baoheng was demoted again to magistrate of Chengmai in Yazhou, and soon was granted permission to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Baoheng was demoted again, to magistrate of Chengmai in Yazhou, and shortly afterward was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 又貶其弟翰林學士、兵部侍郎保乂爲賓州司戸，所親翰林學士、戸部侍郎劉承雍爲涪州司馬。

translations.literal: His younger brother Baoyi, a Hanlin academician and vice minister of war, was demoted to registrar of Binzhou; his confidant Liu Chengyong, Hanlin academician and vice minister of revenue, was demoted to defender of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Baoyi, a Hanlin scholar and vice minister of war, was reduced to registrar of Bin prefecture; his confidant Liu Chengyong, likewise a Hanlin scholar and vice minister of revenue, was made defender of Fu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 承雍，禹錫之子也。

translations.literal: Chengyong was the son of Liu Yuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyong was the son of the poet Liu Yuxi.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，赦天下。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day, the empire was granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使路巖，喜聲色-{游}-宴，委軍府政事-{於}-親吏邊-{鹹}-、郭籌，皆先行-{後}-申，上下畏之。
