translations.literal: Lu Yan, military commissioner of Sichuan, delighted in music, women, and revelry, and entrusted military and administrative affairs to his trusted clerks Bian Xian and Guo Chou, who always acted first and reported afterward; superiors and subordinates alike feared them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yan, the Sichuan military commissioner, indulged in pleasure, music, and feasting, leaving military and civil affairs to his cronies Bian Xian and Guo Chou, who acted first and asked permission later. Everyone above and below them lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 嘗大閲，二人議事，默書紙相示而焚之，軍中以爲有異圖，驚懼不安。

translations.literal: Once during a grand review, the two men discussed business, silently writing on paper, showing it to each other, and burning it. The army thought they harbored ulterior designs and was alarmed and uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: During one grand inspection they conferred by writing silently on paper, showing each other what they had written and then burning it. The troops took this for plotting and grew frightened and restless.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，十一月，戊辰，徙巖荊南節度使。

translations.literal: When the court heard of this, in the eleventh month, on the day wuchen, Lu Yan was transferred to military commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the capital, Lu Yan was transferred in the eleventh month, on the wuchen day, to military commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: -{鹹}-、籌潛知其故，遂亡命。

translations.literal: Xian and Chou secretly understood the reason and fled for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Xian and Chou guessed why he had been moved and went on the run.

sentences.zh: 以右-{僕}-射蕭鄴同平章事，充河東節度使。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Xiao Ye was made Concurrent Grand Councillor and Military Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ye, right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed grand councillor and military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 十二月，巳亥，詔送佛骨還法門寺。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day jihai, an edict ordered the Buddha's bone relic returned to Famen Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the jihai day, an edict commanded that the Buddha's bone relic be sent back to Famen Temple.

sentences.zh: 再貶路巖爲新州刺史。

translations.literal: Lu Yan was demoted again to prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yan was demoted yet again, to prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 僖宗惠聖恭定孝皇帝上之上

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong Huishèng Gongding Xiao — Upper, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong — Upper Segment, Part One

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁亥，翰林學士盧攜上言，以爲：「陛下初臨大寶，宜深念黎元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day dinghai, Hanlin Academician Lu Xi submitted a memorial, stating: "Your Majesty has only just ascended the great throne; you should deeply consider the welfare of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on the dinghai day, Hanlin Academician Lu Xi memorialized the throne: "Your Majesty has only just taken power; you must keep the people's welfare close to your heart.

sentences.zh: 國家之有百姓，如草木之有根柢，若秋冬培溉，則春夏滋榮。

translations.literal: A state has the common people as plants have roots and stems: if nourished and watered in autumn and winter, they flourish in spring and summer.
translations.idiomatic: A state depends on its people the way plants depend on their roots—nurture them through hard seasons, and they will flourish when times turn fair.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見關東去年旱災，自虢至海，麥-{才}-半收，秋稼-{幾}-無，冬菜至少，貧者磑蓬實爲-{面}-，蓄槐-{葉}-爲齏。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed that east of the Pass suffered drought last year; from Guo to the sea, wheat yielded only half a harvest, autumn crops were nearly absent, and winter vegetables were very scarce. The poor ground thistle seeds for flour and stored pagoda-tree leaves for pickle.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen how drought struck east of the Pass last year: from Guo to the sea, wheat brought in only half a crop, autumn grain nearly failed, and winter greens were almost nonexistent. The poor ground thistle seeds into flour and hoarded pagoda-tree leaves for relish.

sentences.zh: 或更衰贏，亦難採拾。

translations.literal: Some were so enfeebled that even gathering such things was difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Some were so weakened by hunger that they could barely gather even that much.

sentences.zh: 常年不稔，則散之鄰境。

translations.literal: In ordinary years of poor harvest, people dispersed into neighboring districts.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary lean years people could still move into neighboring regions.

sentences.zh: 今所在皆饑，無所依投，坐守鄕閭，待盡溝壑。

translations.literal: Now hunger prevailed everywhere; there was nowhere to flee for refuge. People remained in their villages, waiting to perish in ditches and gullies.
translations.idiomatic: Now famine was everywhere at once. There was nowhere left to flee, and people stayed in their home villages, waiting to die in the gutters.

translations.literal: As for remitted and exempted remaining taxes, in truth there was nothing left to collect.
translations.idiomatic: Even remitted and forgiven taxes could not in truth be collected—there was simply nothing left to take.

sentences.zh: 而州縣以有上供及三司錢，督趣甚急，動如捶撻，雖撤屋伐木，雇妻鬻子，止可供所由酒食之費，未得至-{於}-府庫也。

translations.literal: Yet prefectures and counties, owing to tribute quotas and funds owed the Three Departments, pressed collection with extreme urgency, often with beatings. Even tearing down houses and felling trees, hiring out wives and selling children brought in only enough to cover the clerks' food and drink—not enough to reach the government treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Yet local officials, pressed for tribute and payments to the Three Departments, demanded collection with brutal urgency. Families might tear down their houses, sell timber, hire out wives, or sell children—and still raise only enough to feed the runners who came to collect, never enough to fill the government coffers.

sentences.zh: 或租稅之外，更有他徭。

translations.literal: Beyond rent and tax, there were further corvée obligations.
translations.idiomatic: On top of rent and taxes came other forced levies.

sentences.zh: 朝廷倘不撫存，百姓實無生計。

translations.literal: If the court did not succor and preserve them, the common people truly had no means of living.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the court stepped in to relieve them, the people had no way to survive.

sentences.zh: 乞敕州縣，應所欠殘稅，-{並}-一切停-{-{征}-}-，以俟蠶麥。

translations.literal: I beg that prefectures and counties be ordered to suspend entirely all collection of outstanding and residual taxes, pending the silk and wheat harvests.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that every county and prefecture be commanded to halt all collection of unpaid and residual taxes until the mulberry and wheat harvests come in.

sentences.zh: 仍-{發}-所在義倉，亟加賑給。

translations.literal: Local relief granaries should also be opened and urgent relief distributed.
translations.idiomatic: Open the local emergency granaries and distribute aid at once.

sentences.zh: 至深春之-{後}-，有菜-{葉}-木牙，繼以桑椹，漸有可食。

translations.literal: After deep spring there would be vegetable leaves and tree buds, followed by mulberries, and food would gradually become available.
translations.idiomatic: After late spring there would be wild greens and tree shoots, then mulberries—food would slowly become available again.

sentences.zh: 在今數月之間，尤爲窘急，行之不可稽緩。」

translations.literal: Within the next few months the need was especially desperate; this must be carried out without delay."
translations.idiomatic: The next few months will be the worst of it. This cannot wait.

sentences.zh: 敕從其言，而有司竟不能行，徒爲空文而己。

translations.literal: An edict accepted his proposal, but the responsible offices in the end could not implement it—it remained mere empty words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed by edict, but the responsible offices never carried it out. The order stayed on paper and nowhere else.

sentences.zh: 路巖行至江陵，敕削官爵，長流儋州。

translations.literal: When Lu Yan reached Jiangling, an edict stripped him of rank and banished him in perpetuity to Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Yan reached Jiangling, an edict stripped him of rank and exiled him for life to Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 巖美姿儀，囚-{於}-江陵獄再宿，-{鬚}--{髮}-皆白，尋賜自盡，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Yan was handsome in bearing. After two nights imprisoned in the Jiangling jail, his beard and hair all turned white. He was soon granted permission to commit suicide, and his family's property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had been a strikingly handsome man. Two nights in the Jiangling jail turned his hair and beard white. He was soon ordered to kill himself, and his family's property was seized.

sentences.zh: 巖之爲相也，密奏，「三品以上賜死，皆令使者剔取結喉三寸以進，驗其必死。」

translations.literal: When Yan had served as chief minister, he had secretly memorialized: "When persons of the third rank and above are granted death by suicide, the envoy should be ordered to cut out three inches of the larynx and submit it, to verify that death is certain."
translations.idiomatic: While serving as chief minister, Yan had secretly proposed that whenever anyone of third rank or above was granted suicide, the envoy should cut out three inches of the throat and send it back, to prove death was certain.

sentences.zh: 至是，自罹其禍，所死之處乃楊收賜死之榻也。

translations.literal: Now he himself suffered that fate, and the couch on which he died was the very one on which Yang Shou had been granted suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Now he met the same fate himself—and died on the very couch where Yang Shou had been forced to take his life.

sentences.zh: 邊-{鹹}-、郭籌捕得，皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Bian Xian and Guo Chou were captured and both executed.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Xian and Guo Chou were captured and put to death.

sentences.zh: 初，巖佐崔鉉-{於}-淮南，爲支使，鉉知其必貴，曰：「路十終須作彼一官。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yan had served under Cui Xuan in Huainan as a branch commissioner, Xuan knew he was destined for greatness and said: "Lu Ten will eventually hold that particular office."
translations.idiomatic: Long before, when Yan had served under Cui Xuan in Huainan as a branch commissioner, Xuan saw his future clearly and said, "Lu Ten is bound for that highest office one day.

sentences.zh: 既而入爲監察-{御}-史，不出長安城，十年至宰相。

translations.literal: He then entered service as an investigating censor, never leaving Chang'an, and within ten years reached the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to investigating censor, never left Chang'an, and within ten years became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 其自監察入翰林也，鉉猶在淮南，聞之，曰：「路十今已入翰林，如何得老！」

translations.literal: When he entered the Hanlin Academy from the censorate, Xuan was still in Huainan and heard of it, saying: "Lu Ten has now entered the Hanlin—how can he grow old in peace!"
translations.idiomatic: When he entered the Hanlin from the censorate, Xuan was still in Huainan and exclaimed, "Lu Ten is in the Hanlin now—he'll never be allowed to die in his bed!

sentences.zh: 皆如鉉言。

translations.literal: All came to pass just as Xuan had said.
translations.idiomatic: Everything happened exactly as Xuan had predicted.

sentences.zh: 以太子少傅-{-{于}-}-琮同平章事，充山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: Yu Cong, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was made Concurrent Grand Councillor and Military Commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Cong, grand mentor of the heir apparent, was appointed grand councillor and military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲午，葬昭聖恭惠孝皇帝-{於}-簡陵，廟號懿宗。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day jiawu, Emperor Zhaosheng Gonghui Xiao was buried at Jian Mausoleum; his temple name was Yizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the jiawu day, the late emperor was buried at Jian Mausoleum and given the temple name Yizong.

sentences.zh: 以中書侍郎、同平章事趙隱同平章事，充鎭海節度使；

translations.literal: Zhao Yin, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Councillor, was appointed Concurrent Grand Councillor and Military Commissioner of Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yin, vice director of the Secretariat and grand councillor, was confirmed as grand councillor and named military commissioner of Zhenhai;

sentences.zh: 以華州刺史裴坦爲中書侍郎、同平章事；

translations.literal: Pei Tan, prefect of Hua, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Tan, prefect of Hua, was made vice director of the Secretariat and grand councillor;

sentences.zh: 以虢州刺史劉瞻爲刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Liu Zhan, prefect of Guo, was made Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan, prefect of Guo, was appointed minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 瞻之貶也，人無賢愚，莫不痛惜。

translations.literal: When Zhan was demoted, whether wise or foolish, none did not grieve for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhan was demoted, everyone—from the wise to the simple—mourned the loss.

sentences.zh: 及其還也，長安兩市人率錢雇百戲迎之。

translations.literal: When he returned, the people of both market wards of Chang'an pooled money to hire entertainers to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the capital, people from both markets of Chang'an pooled money to hire street performers to welcome him home.

sentences.zh: 瞻聞之，改期，由他道而入。

translations.literal: When Zhan heard of this, he changed his arrival date and entered by another route.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan heard of the plan, changed his schedule, and entered the city by a different road.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，乙未，裴坦薨。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the day yiwei, Pei Tan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, on the yiwei day, Pei Tan died.

sentences.zh: 以劉瞻爲中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Liu Zhan was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 初，瞻南遷，劉鄴附-{於}-韋、路，共短之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhan was banished south, Liu Ye had attached himself to Wei and Lu and joined in slandering him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhan had been exiled south, Liu Ye had attached himself to Wei Baoheng and Lu Yan and helped blacken his name.

sentences.zh: 及瞻還爲相，鄴内懼。

translations.literal: When Zhan returned as chief minister, Ye was inwardly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhan returned as chief minister, Liu Ye was terrified.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，丁巳朔，鄴延瞻，置酒-{於}-鹽鐵院。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on the first day dingsi, Ye invited Zhan to linger and set out wine at the Salt and Iron Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, on the first day of the month, Liu Ye invited Liu Zhan to linger and treated him to wine at the Salt and Iron Commission.

sentences.zh: 瞻歸而遇疾，辛未，薨。

translations.literal: Zhan returned home and fell ill; on the day xinwei, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan went home and fell ill; on the xinwei day he was dead.

sentences.zh: 時人皆以爲鄴鴆之也。

translations.literal: People of the time all believed Ye had poisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time everyone believed Liu Ye had poisoned him.

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎、判度支崔彦昭爲中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Cui Yanzhao, Vice Minister of War and Acting Director of the Fiscal Affairs Section, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanzhao, vice minister of war and acting head of fiscal affairs, was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 彦昭，群之從子也。

translations.literal: Yanzhao was a cousin's son of Cui Qun.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao was a nephew of Cui Qun.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎王凝，正雅之從孫也，其母，彦昭之從母。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Wang Ning was a grand-nephew of Wang Zhengya; his mother was Yanzhao's mother's sister.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Wang Ning was a grand-nephew of Wang Zhengya; his mother was Yanzhao's aunt.

sentences.zh: 凝、彦昭同舉進士，凝先及第，嘗衩衣見彦昭，且戲之曰：「君不若舉明經。」

translations.literal: Ning and Yanzhao took the jinshi examination together; Ning passed first. Once, wearing an unseemly coat, he came to see Yanzhao and joked: "You would do better to try the mingjing examination."
translations.idiomatic: Ning and Yanzhao had taken the jinshi exam together, and Ning had passed first. Once Ning came to see Yanzhao dressed in a slovenly coat and taunted him, "You'd be better off taking the mingjing exam instead.

sentences.zh: 彦昭怒，遂爲深仇。

translations.literal: Yanzhao was enraged, and thereafter they became bitter enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao flew into a rage, and from that day they were mortal enemies.

sentences.zh: 及彦昭爲相，其母謂侍婢曰：「爲我多作襪履，王侍郎母子必將竄逐，吾當與妹偕行。」

translations.literal: When Yanzhao became chief minister, his mother said to her maidservant: "Make many socks and shoes for me. Vice Minister Wang and his mother are sure to be driven into exile, and I shall travel together with my sister."
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhao became chief minister, his mother told a maid, "Make plenty of socks and shoes. Vice Minister Wang and his mother will surely be driven out—I will go into exile with my sister.

sentences.zh: 彦昭拜且泣，謝曰：「必不敢。」

translations.literal: Yanzhao bowed and wept, apologizing: "I surely will not dare."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao bowed, weeping, and swore, "I would never dare.

sentences.zh: 凝由是獲免。

translations.literal: Ning thereby escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ning was spared.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，以門下侍郎、同平章事劉鄴同平章事，充淮南節度使。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Liu Ye, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Concurrent Grand Councillor, was appointed Concurrent Grand Councillor and Military Commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, Liu Ye, vice director of the chancellery and grand councillor, was confirmed as grand councillor and sent out as military commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 以吏部侍郎鄭畋爲兵部侍郎，翰林學士承旨、戸部侍郎盧攜守本官，-{並}-同平章事。

translations.literal: Zheng Tian, Vice Director of the Department of Personnel, was made Vice Minister of War; Lu Xi, Hanlin Academician Expositor and Vice Minister of Revenue, retained his existing posts—and both were made Concurrent Grand Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tian was moved from vice director of personnel to vice minister of war; Lu Xi kept his posts as Hanlin expositor and vice minister of revenue—and both men were appointed grand councillors.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚寅，日南至，群臣上尊號曰聖神聰睿仁哲孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day gengyin, the winter solstice, the assembled ministers offered the honorific title Sacred, Divine, Sagacious, Wise, Benevolent, and Filial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the gengyin day—the winter solstice—the court offered Emperor Xizong the honorific "Sacred, Divine, Sagacious, Wise, Benevolent, and Filial."

sentences.zh: 改元。

translations.literal: The reign era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: The reign title was changed.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使韓允中薨，軍中立其子節度副使簡爲留-{後}-。

translations.literal: Weibo military commissioner Han Yunzhong died; the army installed his son, Vice Commissioner Jian, as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yunzhong, military commissioner of Weibo, died; the troops made his son Jian, the deputy commissioner, acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 南詔寇西川，作浮梁，濟大渡河。

translations.literal: Nanzhao raided Sichuan, built a pontoon bridge, and crossed the Dadu River.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao invaded Sichuan, threw a pontoon bridge across the Dadu River, and crossed.

sentences.zh: 防河都知兵馬使、黎州刺史黃景-{復}-俟其半濟，撃之，蠻敗走，斷其浮梁。

translations.literal: Huang Jingfu, Commander-in-Chief for River Defense and prefect of Li, waited until they were half across, then attacked; the barbarians were defeated and fled, and the pontoon bridge was cut.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jingfu, river-defense commander and prefect of Li, waited until the raiders were halfway across, then struck. The enemy broke and fled, and he cut the pontoon bridge behind them.

sentences.zh: 蠻以中軍多張旗幟當其前，而分兵潛出上、下流各二十-{里}-，夜，作浮梁，詰朝，倶濟，襲破諸城柵，夾攻景-{復}-。

translations.literal: The barbarians put many banners in the center army to block the front, while secretly sending detachments twenty li upstream and downstream; by night they built pontoon bridges, and at dawn all crossed, stormed and broke the various fortifications, and attacked Jingfu from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanzhao army massed banners in the center to hold Huang's attention while secretly sending columns twenty li upstream and downstream. They built pontoon bridges by night; at dawn both forces were across, overran the border forts, and closed on Huang Jingfu from two sides.

sentences.zh: 力戰三日，景-{復}-陽敗走，蠻盡鋭追之。

translations.literal: After three days of hard fighting, Jingfu feigned defeat and fled; the barbarians pursued at full strength.
translations.idiomatic: After three days of fierce fighting, Huang Jingfu feigned defeat and withdrew; the enemy threw everything they had into the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 景-{復}-設三伏以待之，蠻過三分之二，乃-{發}-伏撃之，蠻兵大敗，殺二千-{餘}-人，追至大渡河南而還。

translations.literal: Jingfu set three ambushes to await them; when more than two-thirds of the barbarians had passed, the ambush was sprung; the barbarian army was routed, more than two thousand were killed, and the pursuit continued to the south bank of the Dadu before they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jingfu laid three ambushes along the route. When more than two-thirds of the enemy column had passed, he struck. The Nanzhao army was shattered—over two thousand dead—and he chased them to the south bank of the Dadu before turning back.

sentences.zh: -{復}-修完城柵而守之。

translations.literal: He then restored and repaired the fortifications and held them.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the border forts and held the line.

sentences.zh: 蠻歸，至之羅-{谷}-，遇國中-{發}-兵繼至，新舊相合，鉦鼓聲聞數十-{里}-。

translations.literal: As the barbarians withdrew to Zhiluo Valley, reinforcements dispatched from their country arrived; old and new forces combined, and the clang of gongs and drums could be heard for dozens of li.
translations.idiomatic: On the retreat to Zhiluo Valley, fresh troops from the Nanzhao heartland joined them. Old and new armies merged, and the thunder of gongs and drums carried for dozens of li.

sentences.zh: -{復}-寇大渡河，與唐夾水而軍，詐-{雲}-求和，又自上下流潛濟，與景-{復}-戰連日。

translations.literal: They again raided at the Dadu River, encamped facing Tang forces across the water, falsely claimed to seek peace, and also secretly crossed upstream and downstream, fighting Jingfu for many days.
translations.idiomatic: They struck again at the Dadu, camped on the opposite bank from the Tang forces, pretended to sue for peace, and meanwhile slipped troops across upstream and downstream to fight Huang Jingfu day after day.

sentences.zh: 西川援軍不至，而蠻衆日益，景-{復}-不能支，軍遂潰。

translations.literal: Sichuan reinforcements did not arrive, while barbarian numbers daily increased; Jingfu could not hold, and the army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan reinforcements never came, the enemy kept growing stronger, and Huang Jingfu could not hold. His army broke.

sentences.zh: 十二月，党項、回鶻寇天德軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Tangut and Uyghur forces raided the Tiande Army garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Tangut and Uyghur raiders attacked the Tiande garrison.

sentences.zh: 感化軍奏群盜寇掠，州縣不能禁。

translations.literal: The Ganhua Army reported that bandit gangs were plundering and prefectures and counties could not suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ganhua garrison reported that roving bandits were pillaging the countryside and local authorities could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 敕兗、鄆等道出兵討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yan, Yun, and other circuits to dispatch troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Yan, Yun, and neighboring circuits to send troops against the bandits.

sentences.zh: 南詔乘勝陷黎州，入邛峽關，攻雅州。

translations.literal: Nanzhao, riding victory, captured Lizhou, entered Qiongxia Pass, and attacked Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing their advantage, Nanzhao seized Lizhou, pushed through Qiongxia Pass, and assaulted Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 大渡河潰兵奔入邛州，成都驚擾，民爭入城，或北奔他州。

translations.literal: Routed troops from the Dadu River fled into Qiongzhou; Chengdu was alarmed and thrown into turmoil, the people scrambling to enter the city, some fleeing north to other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers routed at the Dadu River poured into Qiongzhou. Panic swept Chengdu as people fought to get inside the walls or fled north to neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 城中大爲守備，而塹壘比向時嚴固。

translations.literal: Within the city, defenses were greatly strengthened, and trenches and ramparts were more secure than before.
translations.idiomatic: The city girded itself for siege; ditches and earthworks were thrown up far more formidable than ever before.

sentences.zh: 驃信使其坦綽遺節度使牛叢書-{云}-：「非敢爲寇也，欲入見天子，-{面}-訴數十年爲讒人離間冤抑之事。

translations.literal: King Piluoge sent his envoy Tan Chuo with a message to Military Commissioner Niu Congshu, saying: "We do not dare to act as raiders; we wish to enter and see the Son of Heaven and personally appeal the wrongs of decades of slander and estrangement by malicious men.
translations.idiomatic: King Piluoge dispatched Tan Chuo to Military Commissioner Niu Congshu with a letter proclaiming: "We mean no invasion—we wish only to journey east to audience with the Son of Heaven and plead face to face the grievances of thirty years, when slanderers drove us apart and wrongfully suppressed us.

sentences.zh: 倘蒙聖恩矜恤，當還與尚書永敦鄰好。

translations.literal: If we may receive the Sage's gracious pity, we shall return and forever maintain neighborly friendship with the Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Should Your Majesty extend his mercy, we shall withdraw and forever renew our bonds of peace with your court.

sentences.zh: 今假道貴府，欲借蜀王廳留止數日，即東上。」

translations.literal: We now ask passage through your noble prefecture, wish to borrow the Prince of Shu's hall to halt for several days, then proceed east."
translations.idiomatic: We seek passage through your jurisdiction and ask leave to lodge for a few days in the Prince of Shu's hall, then continue eastward."

sentences.zh: 叢素懦怯，欲許之，楊慶-{復}-以爲不可。

translations.literal: Cong had long been timid and cowardly and wished to agree; Yang Qingfu believed this unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Cong, a man of habitual timidity, was inclined to consent; Yang Qingfu insisted it must not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 斬其使者，留二人，授以書，遣還，書辭極數其罪，詈辱之。

translations.literal: He executed their envoys, kept two men, gave them a letter, and sent them back; the letter's language exhaustively enumerated their crimes and reviled and shamed them.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded the envoys, detained two of their party, handed them a reply bristling with indictments, and sent them back in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 蠻兵及新津而還，叢恐蠻至，豫焚城外，民居蕩盡，蜀人尤之。

translations.literal: Barbarian troops reached Xinjin and withdrew; Cong, fearing the barbarians would come, preemptively burned outside the walls, and common dwellings were utterly destroyed; the people of Shu blamed him severely.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian army withdrew after reaching Xinjin. Fearful they would return, Cong ordered the suburbs burned preemptively, reducing countless homes to ash—and the people of Shu never forgave him.

sentences.zh: 詔-{發}-河東、山南西道、東川兵援之，仍命天平節度使髙駢詣西川-{制}-置蠻事。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched troops from Hedong, the Western Section of Shannan, and Dongchuan to reinforce them, and still appointed Tianping Military Commissioner Gao Pian to proceed to Sichuan to manage barbarian affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict mobilized reinforcements from Hedong, Western Shannan, and Dongchuan, and charged Tianping Military Commissioner Gao Pian with overall command of the barbarian campaign in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 以韓簡爲魏博留-{後}-。

translations.literal: Han Jian was made acting commissioner of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian was appointed acting military commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 商州刺史王樞以軍州空窘，減折糴錢，民相帥以白梃毆之，又毆殺官吏二人。

translations.literal: Shangzhou Prefect Wang Shu, because the army and prefecture were destitute and straitened, reduced the price for government grain purchases; the people rallied together and beat him with clubs, and also beat to death two officials.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu, prefect of Shangzhou, slashed the rate for compulsory grain purchases because his district was bankrupt. The populace rose up, clubbed him, and killed two of his officials.

sentences.zh: 朝廷更除刺史李誥到官，收捕民李叔汶等三十人，斬之。

translations.literal: The court replaced him with Prefect Li Gao, who upon taking office seized and arrested thirty men including the commoner Li Shuwen and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The court replaced Wang with Li Gao, who upon arrival arrested Li Shuwen and twenty-nine others and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 初，回鶻屢求冊命，詔遣冊立使郗宗莒詣其國。

translations.literal: Previously, the Uyghurs had repeatedly sought investiture; an edict dispatched enfoffment envoy Xi Zongju to their country.
translations.idiomatic: For some time the Uyghurs had petitioned repeatedly for formal investiture. The throne dispatched Xi Zongju as envoy to confer it.

sentences.zh: 會回鶻爲吐-{谷}-渾、嗢末所破，逃遁不知所之。

translations.literal: Just then the Uyghurs were destroyed by the Tuyuhun and Wamo, and fled in flight, their whereabouts unknown.
translations.idiomatic: But before he arrived, the Uyghurs were shattered by the Tuyuhun and Wamo and scattered—their fate unknown.

sentences.zh: 詔宗莒以玉冊、國信授靈鹽節度使唐弘夫掌之，還京師。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zongju to entrust the jade edict and credentials of state to Lingzhou-Yanzhou Military Commissioner Tang Hongfu for safekeeping, and return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zongju was ordered to leave the jade register and imperial credentials with Ling-Yan Military Commissioner Tang Hongfu and return to court.

sentences.zh: 上年少，政在臣下，南牙、北司互相矛楯。

translations.literal: The Emperor was young; government lay with his ministers; the Southern Bureau and Northern Bureau opposed each other like spear and shield.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still a boy; power rested with his ministers, while the regular bureaucracy and the eunuch directorates locked horns like spear against shield.

sentences.zh: 自懿宗以來，奢侈日甚，用兵不息，賦斂愈急。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Yizong, extravagance daily increased, warfare unceasing, tax levies ever more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Since the reign of Emperor Yizong, extravagance had grown unchecked, wars had never ceased, and exactions had grown harsher by the year.

sentences.zh: 關東連年水、旱，州縣不以實聞，上下相蒙，百姓流殍，無所控訴。

translations.literal: East of the Pass suffered flood and drought year after year; prefectures and counties did not report the truth; superiors and subordinates deceived one another; the people wandered in starvation; there was nowhere to lodge grievances.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Pass, flood and drought struck year after year, yet local officials lied to the throne and the court lied to itself. The starving had nowhere to turn for justice.

sentences.zh: 相聚爲盜，所在蜂起。

translations.literal: They gathered together to become bandits; everywhere they swarmed up like bees.
translations.idiomatic: Desperate men banded together as outlaws; uprisings erupted everywhere.

sentences.zh: 州縣兵少，加以承平日久，人不習戰，毎與盜遇，官軍多敗。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties had few troops; moreover, after long peace, people were unaccustomed to war; whenever they met bandits, government armies mostly lost.
translations.idiomatic: County garrisons were thin, and a generation of peace had left soldiers untrained. Time and again imperial troops met bandits and were routed.

sentences.zh: 是歳，濮州人王仙芝始聚衆數千，起-{於}-長垣。

translations.literal: That year, Wang Xianzhi of Puzhou first gathered several thousand men and rose at Changyuan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang Xianzhi of Puzhou assembled several thousand followers and raised the standard of rebellion at Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙戌，以髙駢爲西川節度使。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day bingxu, Gao Pian was made Military Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on bingxu day in the first month, Gao Pian was appointed military commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 辛已，上祀圓丘；

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, the Emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound;
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day the emperor performed the Round Mound sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: He pardoned the empire.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was declared throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 髙駢至劍州，先遣使走馬開成都門。

translations.literal: Gao Pian reached Jianzhou and first dispatched a messenger at full gallop to open the gates of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Pian reached Jianzhou, he sent a rider ahead at full gallop to order Chengdu's gates opened.

sentences.zh: 或諫曰：「蠻寇逼近成都，相公尚遠，萬一豨突，奈何？」

translations.literal: Someone remonstrated: "Barbarian raiders are close to Chengdu, yet the Lord Commissioner is still far away—if they should suddenly charge, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: An adviser warned: "Barbarian raiders are almost upon Chengdu, and you are still far off. What if they strike before you arrive?"

sentences.zh: 駢曰：「吾在交趾破蠻二十萬衆，蠻聞我來，逃竄不暇，何敢輒犯成都！

translations.literal: Pian said: "I broke two hundred thousand barbarians in Jiaozhi; when the barbarians hear I am coming, they flee without pause—how dare they rashly violate Chengdu!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian replied: "At Jiaozhi I shattered two hundred thousand of them. When they hear I am coming they will flee headlong—how would they dare touch Chengdu!

sentences.zh: 今春氣向暖，數十萬人蘊積城中，生死共處，汚穢郁蒸，將成癘疫，不可緩也！」

translations.literal: Now spring warmth is approaching; several hundred thousand people are pent up in the city, living and dying together, filth steaming and stagnant—it will become plague. This cannot be delayed!"
translations.idiomatic: Spring is warming. Hundreds of thousands are packed inside those walls, living atop their own filth—plague will break out if we do not act at once!"

sentences.zh: 使者至成都，開城縱民出，各-{復}-常業，乘城者皆下城解甲，民大悅。

translations.literal: When the messenger reached Chengdu, the gates were opened and the people allowed out; each returned to his usual occupation; those manning the walls all came down and laid aside arms; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: His messenger reached Chengdu, the gates swung open, and the populace poured out to resume their livelihoods. Defenders climbed down and doffed their armor. Joy swept the city.

sentences.zh: 蠻方攻雅州，聞之，遣使請和，引兵去。

translations.literal: The barbarians were attacking Yazhou; hearing this, they sent envoys seeking peace and withdrew their troops.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians, then besieging Yazhou, sent envoys suing for peace and marched away.

sentences.zh: 駢又奏：「南蠻小-{丑}-，易以枝梧。

translations.literal: Pian further memorialized: "The southern barbarians are petty rabble, easily managed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian memorialized further: "These southern savages are a petty nuisance, easily handled.

sentences.zh: 今西川新舊兵已多，所-{發}-長武、鄜坊、河東兵，徒有勞費，-{並}-乞勒還。」

translations.literal: Now Sichuan's old and new troops are already numerous; the troops dispatched from Changwu, Fufang, and Hedong are but wasted labor and expense—I beg that all be ordered to return."
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan already has ample forces. The contingents sent from Changwu, Fufang, and Hedong only drain the treasury—forbid their march and send them home."

sentences.zh: 敕止河東兵而己。

translations.literal: An edict halted only the Hedong troops.
translations.idiomatic: The throne recalled only the Hedong contingent.

sentences.zh: 上之爲普王也，小馬坊使田令孜有寵，及即位，使知樞密，遂擢爲中尉。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was Prince of Pu, Remount Office Commissioner Tian Lingzi had favor; upon his accession, he was made Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and then promoted to Chief Eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: While still Prince of Pu, the future emperor had favored Tian Lingzi, commissioner of the Pony Yard. Upon his accession Tian was put in charge of secret military affairs, then elevated to chief eunuch.

sentences.zh: 上時年十四，專事-{遊}-戲，政事一委令孜，呼爲「阿父」。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then fourteen sui, devoted entirely to play; all government he entrusted to Lingzi, calling him "Uncle."
translations.idiomatic: The boy emperor was fourteen. He gave himself over to games and amusements, handed all affairs of state to Tian Lingzi, and called him "Father."

sentences.zh: 令孜頗讀書，多巧數，招權納賄，除官及賜緋紫皆不關白-{於}-上。

translations.literal: Lingzi read books considerably, employed many crafty stratagems, sought power and accepted bribes; appointments and bestowals of red and purple rank robes were never reported to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Tian was literate and cunning, amassing power through bribery. He appointed officials and awarded emblems of rank without ever consulting the throne.

sentences.zh: 毎見，常自備果食兩盤，與上相對飲啖，從容良久而退。

translations.literal: Whenever he attended audience, he always brought two plates of fruit and food himself, ate and drank facing the Emperor, and leisurely withdrew after a long while.
translations.idiomatic: At each audience he arrived bearing two trays of delicacies, shared a leisurely meal with the young emperor, and only then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上與内園小兒狎暱，賞賜樂工、伎兒，所費動以萬計，府藏空竭。

translations.literal: The Emperor was intimate with the inner-garden youths; rewards to musicians and performers routinely ran to tens of thousands; the treasury was emptied.
translations.idiomatic: He grew intimate with the palace child attendants, showering musicians and performers with gifts that ran to ten thousand strings of cash—and drained the treasury dry.

sentences.zh: 令孜説上籍兩市商旅寶貨悉輸内庫，有陳訴者，付京兆杖殺之。

translations.literal: Lingzi persuaded the Emperor to register the merchants of both markets and have all their goods and treasures sent to the inner treasury; those who lodged complaints were handed to the metropolitan prefect to be beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Tian persuaded the emperor to seize the goods of every merchant in both markets for the palace vaults. Complaints were referred to the metropolitan prefect, who had the complainants beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 宰相以下，鉗口莫敢言。

translations.literal: From the chief ministers downward, mouths were clamped shut and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: From the chief ministers down, not a voice was raised in protest.

sentences.zh: 髙駢至成都，明日，-{發}-歩騎五千追南詔，至大渡河，殺獲甚衆，擒其酋長數十人，至成都，斬之。

translations.literal: Gao Pian reached Chengdu; the next day he dispatched five thousand infantry and cavalry in pursuit of Nanzhao; reaching the Dadu River, he killed and captured in great numbers, seized several dozen chieftains, and upon reaching Chengdu, executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The day after Gao Pian reached Chengdu, he led five thousand foot and horse in pursuit of Nanzhao. At the Dadu River his men slaughtered vast numbers, captured dozens of chieftains, and beheaded them in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 修-{復}-邛崍關、大渡河諸城柵，又-{築}-城-{於}-戎州馬湖鎭，號平夷軍；

translations.literal: He restored Qionglai Pass and the fortifications along the Dadu River, and further built a fortress at Rongzhou's Mahenzhen, named the Pingyi Army;
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt Qionglai Pass and the Dadu River defenses, and erected a fortress at Mahen in Rongzhou, garrisoned as the Pingyi Army;

sentences.zh: 又-{築}-城-{於}-沐源川，皆蠻入蜀之要道也，各置兵數千戍之。

translations.literal: further built a fortress at Moyuan Creek—all key routes by which barbarians entered Shu—each garrisoned with several thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: and fortified Moyuan Creek, a strategic corridor for barbarian incursions into Shu, with several thousand soldiers at each post.

sentences.zh: 自是蠻不-{復}-入寇。

translations.literal: From this the barbarians no longer raided.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao never invaded again.

sentences.zh: 駢召黃景-{復}-，責以大渡河失守，腰斬之。

translations.literal: Pian summoned Huang Jingfu, blamed him for the loss of the Dadu River defense, and cut him in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian summoned Huang Jingfu, held him accountable for the fall of the Dadu River line, and had him executed by waist-slicing.

sentences.zh: 駢又奏請自將本管及天平、昭義、義成等軍共六萬人撃南詔，詔不許。

translations.literal: Pian further memorialized requesting to personally lead his own circuit forces plus Tianping, Zhaoyi, Yicheng, and other armies—sixty thousand men in all—to strike Nanzhao; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He further asked leave to lead sixty thousand men from his own and allied circuits against Nanzhao. The throne refused.

sentences.zh: 先是，南詔督爽屢牒中書，辭語怨望，中書不答。

translations.literal: Previously, Nanzhao's supervising envoy had repeatedly sent dispatches to the Secretariat, language resentful and dissatisfied; the Secretariat did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: For some time Nanzhao's supervisory envoy had bombarded the Secretariat with bitter dispatches. The Secretariat never answered.

sentences.zh: 盧攜奏稱：「如此，則蠻益驕，謂唐無以答，宜數其十代受恩以責之。

translations.literal: Lu Xi memorialized: "If so, the barbarians will grow more arrogant, believing Tang has no reply—it is fitting to enumerate ten generations of received grace to reproach them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xi argued: "Silence only emboldens them—they will conclude Tang has no answer. Recite the ten generations of imperial favor Nanzhao has enjoyed and hold them to account.

sentences.zh: 然自中書-{發}-牒，則嫌-{於}-體敵，請賜髙駢及嶺南西道節度使辛讜詔，使録詔白，牒與之。」

translations.literal: Yet for the Secretariat itself to send dispatches would be improper as treating them as equals—I beg that edicts be granted to Gao Pian and Lingnan West Circuit Military Commissioner Xin Dang, that they read the edicts aloud and dispatch them."
translations.idiomatic: But a dispatch from the Secretariat itself would dignify them as peers. Issue edicts to Gao Pian and Lingnan West Military Commissioner Xin Dang instead, and have them recite the imperial words and deliver the message."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 三月，以魏博留-{後}-韓簡爲節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month, Weibo acting commissioner Han Jian was made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Han Jian was confirmed as military commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 去歳，感化軍-{發}-兵詣靈武防秋，會南詔寇西川，敕往救援。

translations.literal: The previous year, the Ganhua Army dispatched troops to Lingwu for autumn frontier defense; when Nanzhao raided Sichuan, an edict ordered them to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The previous year the Ganhua Army had sent troops to Lingwu for autumn defense. When Nanzhao invaded Sichuan, they were redirected to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 未至成都，蠻退，遣還；

translations.literal: Before reaching Chengdu, the barbarians withdrew, and they were sent back;
translations.idiomatic: Before they reached Chengdu the barbarians withdrew, and they were ordered home;

sentences.zh: 至鳳翔，不肯詣靈武，欲擅歸徐州。

translations.literal: reaching Fengxiang, they refused to go to Lingwu and wished on their own authority to return to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: but at Fengxiang they refused to proceed to Lingwu and tried to march straight back to Xuzhou on their own.

sentences.zh: 内養王裕本、都將劉逢搜擒唱帥者胡雄等八人，斬之，衆然-{後}-定。

translations.literal: Palace Servitor Wang Yuben and Chief Officer Liu Feng searched out and seized the ringleaders including Hu Xiong—eight men—and executed them; only then was the multitude settled.
translations.idiomatic: Palace trainer Wang Yuben and chief officer Liu Feng arrested eight ringleaders led by Hu Xiong and executed them, and only then did the troops quiet down.

sentences.zh: 初，南詔圍成都，楊慶-{復}-以右職優給募突將以-{御}-之，成都由是獲全。

translations.literal: Previously, when Nanzhao besieged Chengdu, Yang Qingfu used high rank and generous pay to recruit shock troops to defend against them; Chengdu thereby was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanzhao besieged Chengdu, Yang Qingfu had recruited crack troops with rank and generous stipends—and thus the city was saved.

sentences.zh: 及髙駢至，悉令納牒，又-{托}-以蜀中屢遭蠻寇，人未-{復}-業，停其稟給，突將皆忿怨。

translations.literal: When Gao Pian arrived, he ordered all to surrender their credentials, and further, citing that Shu had repeatedly suffered barbarian raids and the people had not yet restored their livelihoods, suspended their rations—all the shock troops were resentful and angry.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Pian arrived he stripped them of their commissions, then suspended their pay on the pretext that Shu had not yet recovered from repeated invasions. The shock troops seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 駢好妖-{術}-，毎-{發}-兵追蠻，皆夜張旗立隊，對將士焚紙畫人馬，散小豆，曰：「蜀兵懦怯，今遣玄女神兵前行。」

translations.literal: Pian favored occult arts; whenever he dispatched troops to pursue barbarians, by night he raised banners and formed ranks, facing the officers and soldiers burned paper figures of men and horses, scattered small beans, saying: "Sichuan soldiers are cowardly—I now send the Dark Lady's divine troops ahead."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian dabbled in sorcery. Before every sortie against the barbarians he would parade his troops at night, burn paper effigies of soldiers and horses, scatter beans, and proclaim: "Sichuan men are cowards—so I dispatch the Dark Lady's spirit army ahead."

sentences.zh: 軍中壯士皆恥之。

translations.literal: The stalwart warriors in the army all felt shamed by this.
translations.idiomatic: The veterans were mortified.

sentences.zh: 又索闔境官有出-{於}-胥吏者，皆停之。

translations.literal: He further demanded that throughout the circuit any officials who had risen from clerks all be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He also purged every official in the circuit who had risen from the clerical ranks.

sentences.zh: 令民間皆用足陌錢，陌不足者皆執之，劾以行賂，取與皆死。

translations.literal: He ordered that among the people all use full-value cash; those whose strings fell short were all arrested, charged with bribery—both giver and receiver were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed that all transactions use full-weight coin. Short-weight payments were treated as bribery, and both parties were put to death.

sentences.zh: 刑罰嚴酷，由是蜀人皆不悅。

translations.literal: Punishments were harsh and cruel; thereby the people of Shu were all displeased.
translations.idiomatic: His justice was savage, and discontent spread through Shu.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，突將作亂，大噪突入府廷。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the shock troops rebelled, raising a great clamor and bursting into the headquarters court.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the shock troops mutinied, storming the headquarters in uproar.

sentences.zh: 駢走匿-{於}-廁間，突將索之，不獲。

translations.literal: Pian fled and hid in a privy; the shock troops searched for him but did not find him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian fled and hid in a latrine. The mutineers hunted for him but could not find him.

sentences.zh: 天平都將張傑帥所部數百人被甲入府撃突將，突將撤牙前儀注兵仗，無者奮梃揮拳，乘怒氣力-{鬥}-，天平軍不能敵，走歸營。

translations.literal: Tianping Chief Officer Zhang Jie led several hundred of his men in armor into headquarters to strike the shock troops; the shock troops stripped the ceremonial arms before the headquarters gate; those without weapons seized clubs and swung fists, riding anger and force to fight; the Tianping army could not match them and fled back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jie of Tianping led several hundred armored men into the compound to crush the mutiny. The shock troops grabbed whatever came to hand—ceremonial weapons from the gate, clubs, bare fists—and fought with berserk fury. Zhang's men were beaten back to camp.

sentences.zh: 突將追之，營門閉，不得入。

translations.literal: The shock troops pursued them; the camp gate was closed and they could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers pursued them, but the camp gates were shut against them.

sentences.zh: 監軍使人招諭，許以-{復}-職名稟給，久之，乃肯還營。

translations.literal: The army monitor sent men to summon and instruct them, promising restoration of rank and rations; after a long while, they were willing to return to camp.
translations.idiomatic: The army monitor sent envoys offering restoration of rank and pay. After long negotiation the mutineers agreed to return to quarters.

sentences.zh: 天平軍-{復}-開門出，爲追逐之勢。

translations.literal: The Tianping army again opened the gates and came out, assuming the posture of pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianping troops then sallied forth as if in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 至城北，時方修球塲，役者數百人，天平軍悉取其首，還，詣府，-{云}-「已誅亂者」。

translations.literal: Reaching the north of the city, at that time a ball field was under construction; several hundred laborers—the Tianping army took all their heads, returned, and came to headquarters, saying "We have executed the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Near the north wall they came upon hundreds of laborers building a ball court. The Tianping soldiers beheaded them all, marched back to headquarters, and reported: "The rebels have been exterminated."

sentences.zh: 駢出見之，厚以金帛賞之。

translations.literal: Pian came out to see them and richly rewarded them with gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian emerged and showered them with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 明日，榜謝突將，悉還其職名、衣糧。

translations.literal: The next day he posted a proclamation thanking the shock troops and fully restored their rank and clothing rations.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he posted a placard thanking the shock troops and restored their rank and stipends in full.

sentences.zh: 自是日令諸道將士從己來者更直府中，嚴兵自衞。

translations.literal: From this he daily ordered troops from various circuits who had come with him to rotate guard duty in headquarters, maintaining strict soldiers for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth he kept a rotating guard of troops from his own contingent stationed inside headquarters.

sentences.zh: 加成德節度使王景崇兼侍中。

translations.literal: Chengde Military Commissioner Wang Jingchong was additionally granted the title Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingchong, military commissioner of Chengde, was also made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 浙西狼山鎭遏使王郢等六十九人有戰功，節度使趙隱賞以職名而不給衣糧，郢等論訴不獲，遂劫庫兵作亂，行收黨衆近萬人，攻陷蘇、常，乘舟往來，泛江入海，轉掠二浙，南及福建，大爲人患。

translations.literal: Zhexi Langshan Suppression Commissioner Wang Ying and sixty-nine others had military merit; Military Commissioner Zhao Yin rewarded them with rank titles but gave no clothing and rations; Ying and the others petitioned without success, then seized arsenal weapons and rebelled, gradually gathering nearly ten thousand followers, captured Suzhou and Changzhou, traveled by boat back and forth, sailed the river to the sea, turned to plunder the two Zhe regions, south to Fujian—greatly becoming a bane to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying, suppression commissioner at Langshan in Zhexi, and sixty-eight comrades with battle honors received titles from Military Commissioner Zhao Yin but no pay or provisions. Their petitions went unheard. They raided the armory, raised nearly ten thousand followers, seized Suzhou and Changzhou, and took to the waterways—sailing downriver to the sea and ravaging both Zhes, southward even into Fujian—a scourge upon the land.

sentences.zh: 五月，以太傅、分司令狐綯同平章事，充鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Grand Mentor and Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat Linghu Tao was made Concurrent Grand Councillor and Military Commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Linghu Tao, grand mentor and commissioner of the palace secretariat, was made concurrent grand councillor and military commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 司空、同平章事蕭倣薨。

translations.literal: Minister of Works and Concurrent Grand Councillor Xiao Fang died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fang, minister of works and concurrent grand councillor, died.

sentences.zh: 六月，以-{御}-史大夫李蔚爲中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Censor-in-Chief Li Wei was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Censor-in-Chief Li Wei was appointed vice director of the secretariat and concurrent grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 辛未，髙駢陰籍突將之名，使人夜掩捕之，圍其家，挑牆壞戸而入，老幼孕病，悉驅去殺之，嬰兒或撲-{於}-階，或撃-{於}-柱，流血成渠，號哭震天，死者數千人，夜，以車載屍投之-{於}-江。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Gao Pian secretly registered the names of the shock troops and sent men to seize them by night; surrounding their homes, breaking through walls and doors to enter, old and young, pregnant and sick—all were driven out and killed; infants were dashed on steps or struck against pillars; blood formed channels; wailing shook heaven; several thousand died; by night, carts loaded corpses and cast them into the river.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day Gao Pian secretly compiled a list of shock troop names and sent raiders by night. They broke through walls and doors, dragged out the old, the young, the pregnant, and the sick, and slaughtered them. Infants were dashed against steps and pillars. Blood ran in streams; wails shook the heavens. Several thousand died. That night cartloads of corpses were dumped in the river.

sentences.zh: 有一婦人，臨刑，戟手大罵曰：「髙駢！

translations.literal: One woman, facing execution, pointed her finger and cursed loudly: "Gao Pian!
translations.idiomatic: One woman, at the moment of execution, shook her fist and screamed: "Gao Pian!

sentences.zh: 汝無故奪有功將士職名、衣糧，激成衆怒。

translations.literal: You groundlessly stripped meritorious officers and soldiers of rank and rations, inciting the multitude's rage.
translations.idiomatic: You stripped worthy soldiers of rank and pay without cause and drove them to mutiny.

sentences.zh: 幸而得免，不省己自咎，乃更以詐殺無辜近萬人，天地鬼神，豈容汝如此！

translations.literal: Having luckily escaped, you do not examine yourself and blame yourself, but further by deception kill nearly ten thousand innocents—Heaven and earth, spirits and gods—how could they tolerate you thus!
translations.idiomatic: You escaped only by luck, yet instead of repenting you butchered nearly ten thousand innocents by fraud. Would Heaven and earth, would the gods, suffer such a man to live!

sentences.zh: 我必訴汝-{於}-上帝，使汝他日舉家屠滅如我今日，冤抑汚辱如我今日，驚憂惴恐如我今日！」

translations.literal: I shall surely accuse you before the Supreme Lord, that you another day may have your whole household slaughtered as I today, wrongs and humiliation as I today, alarm, anxiety, dread, and fear as I today!
translations.idiomatic: I will plead your case before the Highest God, that one day your whole house may be butchered as mine is today—wronged, shamed, stricken with terror as I am today!

sentences.zh: 言畢，拜天，怫然就戮。

translations.literal: When she finished speaking, she bowed to Heaven and, scowling, went to execution.
translations.idiomatic: She finished, bowed to Heaven, and marched unflinching to her death.

sentences.zh: 久之，突將有自戍役歸者，駢-{復}-欲盡族之，有元從親吏王殷諫曰：「相公奉道，宜好生惡殺，此屬在外，初不同謀，若-{復}-誅之，則自危者多矣！」

translations.literal: After a long while, shock troops returning from garrison duty—Pian again wished to exterminate their entire clans; his old follower and personal clerk Wang Yin remonstrated: "The Lord Commissioner follows the Way and should cherish life and hate killing; these men were abroad and did not conspire together at first—if you again execute them, many who feel themselves in danger will increase!"
translations.idiomatic: Later, when shock troops began returning from frontier duty, Gao Pian planned to exterminate their entire families. His longtime aide Wang Yin warned: "You profess the Dao, Lord Commissioner—you should cherish life. These men were abroad and had no part in the plot. Slaughter them and how many more will fear for their lives!"

sentences.zh: 駢乃止。

translations.literal: Pian then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian relented.

sentences.zh: 王仙芝及其黨尚君長攻陷濮州、曹州，衆至數萬。

translations.literal: Wang Xianzhi and his follower Shang Junzhang captured Puzhou and Caozhou; their followers reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianzhi and his lieutenant Shang Junzhang seized Puzhou and Caozhou; their following swelled to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 天平節度使薛崇出兵撃之，爲仙芝所敗。

translations.literal: Tianping Military Commissioner Xue Chong dispatched troops to strike them and was defeated by Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Tianping Military Commissioner Xue Chong marched against them and was routed.

sentences.zh: 冤句人黃巣亦聚衆數千人應仙芝。

translations.literal: Huang Chao of Yuanqu also gathered several thousand men and responded to Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao of Yuanqu raised several thousand men and joined Xianzhi's cause.

sentences.zh: 巣少與仙芝皆以販私鹽爲事，巣善騎謝，喜任俠，粗渉書傳，屢舉進士不第，遂爲盜，與仙芝攻剽州縣，橫行山東，民之困-{於}-重斂者爭歸之，數月之間，衆至數萬。

translations.literal: Chao in youth, like Xianzhi, made their living smuggling salt; Chao was skilled at mounted archery, fond of chivalrous daring, had roughly dipped into books and classics, repeatedly failed the jinshi examination, and thus became a bandit; with Xianzhi he attacked and plundered prefectures and counties, rampaged across Shandong; people oppressed by heavy exactions all joined him; within months followers reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In youth both Huang Chao and Wang Xianzhi had smuggled salt. Chao was an expert horseman and archer, a man of reckless honor, with some book learning but repeated failures at the jinshi examinations. He turned outlaw, joined Xianzhi in raiding towns across Shandong, and peasants crushed by taxation flocked to them. Within months their numbers swelled to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 盧龍節度使張公素，性暴戾，不爲軍士所附。

translations.literal: Lulong Military Commissioner Zhang Gongsu was by nature violent and harsh, not adhered to by the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongsu, military commissioner of Lulong, was brutal and held in contempt by his troops.

sentences.zh: 大將李茂勳，本回鶻阿布思之族，回鶻敗，降-{於}-張仲武；

translations.literal: Great General Li Maoxun was originally of the Uyghur Abusi clan; when the Uyghurs were defeated, he surrendered to Zhang Zhongwu;
translations.idiomatic: His chief general Li Maoxun was descended from the Uyghur chieftain Abusi. When the Uyghurs fell, he submitted to Zhang Zhongwu;

sentences.zh: 仲武使戍邊，屢有功，賜姓名。

translations.literal: Zhongwu sent him to garrison the frontier; he repeatedly had merit and was granted a surname and personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu posted him to the frontier, where he won repeated honors and was granted a Chinese name.

sentences.zh: 納降軍使陳貢言者，幽之宿將，爲軍士所信服，茂勳潛殺貢言，聲-{雲}-貢言舉兵向薊；

translations.literal: Chen Gongyan, commissioner of surrendered troops, was an old general of Youzhou, trusted and believed by the soldiers; Maoxun secretly killed Gongyan and proclaimed that Gongyan had raised troops toward Ji;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gongyan, commissioner of surrendered troops, was a veteran of Youzhou deeply trusted by the rank and file. Maoxun murdered him secretly and spread word that Gongyan was marching on Ji;

sentences.zh: 公素出戰而敗，奔京師。

translations.literal: Gongsu went out to battle and was defeated, fleeing to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongsu rode out, was defeated, and fled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 茂勳入城，衆乃知非貢言也，不得已，推而立之，朝廷因以茂勳爲留-{後}-。

translations.literal: Maoxun entered the city; the multitude then knew it was not Gongyan; having no choice, they pushed and established him; the court accordingly made Maoxun acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Maoxun entered the city the troops learned the truth. With no alternative they acclaimed him leader, and the court recognized him as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，蝗自東而西，蔽日，所過赤地。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, locusts from east to west blotted out the sun; where they passed the land was bare red earth.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, locust swarms marched from east to west, blotting out the sun and leaving stripped fields in their wake.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹楊知至奏「蝗入京畿，不食稼，皆抱荊棘而死。」

translations.literal: Metropolitan Prefect Yang Zhizhi memorialized: "Locusts entered the capital region, did not eat crops, but all embraced thorns and brambles and died."
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Prefect Yang Zhizhi reported: "Locusts entered the capital region but ate no grain—they clung to thorn bushes and perished."

sentences.zh: 宰相皆賀。

translations.literal: The chief ministers all congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers offered their congratulations.

sentences.zh: 八月，李茂勳爲盧龍節度使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Li Maoxun was made Military Commissioner of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Li Maoxun was confirmed as military commissioner of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 九月，左補闕董禹諫上-{游}-畋、乘驢撃球，上賜金帛以褒之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Left Remonstrance Officer Dong Yu remonstrated with the Emperor about hunting outings and playing polo while riding a donkey; the Emperor bestowed gold and silk to commend him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Left Remonstrance Officer Dong Yu censured the emperor for pleasure-hunting and for playing polo mounted on a donkey. The emperor rewarded him with gold and silk in praise.

sentences.zh: 邠-{寧}-節度使李侃奏爲假父華淸宮使道雅求贈官，禹上疎論之，語頗侵宦官。

translations.literal: Binning Military Commissioner Li Kan memorialized requesting a posthumous office for his foster father, Huaqing Palace Commissioner Daoya; Yu submitted a memorial arguing against it, his language quite encroaching on the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Binning Military Commissioner Li Kan memorialized asking posthumous honors for his foster father, Huaqing Palace Commissioner Daoya. Dong Yu submitted a counter-memorial, and his language sharply impugned the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 樞密使楊-{復}-恭等列訴-{於}-上，冬，十月，禹坐貶郴州司馬。

translations.literal: Bureau of Military Affairs Director Yang Fugong and others lodged a collective complaint before the Emperor; in winter, the tenth month, Yu was convicted and demoted to Prefectural Aide at Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chief of military affairs Yang Fugong and others filed a joint complaint at court. In the tenth month of winter, Dong Yu was convicted and banished to serve as prefectural aide at Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: -{復}-恭，欽義之養孫也。

translations.literal: Fugong was the adopted grandson of Qinyi.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong was the adopted grandson of Qinyi.

sentences.zh: 昭義軍亂，大將劉廣逐節度使髙湜，自爲留-{後}-。

translations.literal: The Zhaoyi army mutinied; great general Liu Guang drove out Military Commissioner Gao Ni and made himself acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhaoyi garrison mutinied. Chief general Liu Guang expelled Military Commissioner Gao Ni and installed himself as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 以左金吾大將軍曹翔爲昭義節度使。

translations.literal: Left Golden Guard General Cao Xiang was made Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Left Golden Guard General Cao Xiang was appointed military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 回鶻還至羅川，十一月，遣使者同羅楡祿入貢；

translations.literal: The Uyghurs returned to Luochuan; in the eleventh month, they dispatched envoys together with Tongluo Yuyu to come bearing tribute;
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs returned to Luochuan. In the eleventh month they sent envoys, together with the Tongluo chieftain Yuyu, to present tribute at court;

sentences.zh: 賜拯接絹萬匹。

translations.literal: They were granted ten thousand bolts of relief silk.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted them ten thousand bolts of relief silk.

sentences.zh: 群盜侵淫，剽掠十-{餘}-州，至-{於}-淮南，多者千-{餘}-人，少者數百人。

translations.literal: Bandit gangs spread unchecked, plundering more than ten prefectures, reaching as far as Huainan; the larger bands had more than a thousand men, the smaller several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit armies spread unchecked, looting more than ten prefectures and reaching into Huainan. The largest bands numbered over a thousand men; the smallest, several hundred.

sentences.zh: 詔淮南、忠武、宣武、義成、天平五軍節度使、監軍亟加討捕及招懷。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the military commissioners and army supervisors of the five commands—Huainan, Zhongwu, Xuanwu, Yicheng, and Tianping—to press urgently for suppression and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded the military commissioners and army supervisors of Huainan, Zhongwu, Xuanwu, Yicheng, and Tianping to hunt down the bandits at once and win them over where possible.

sentences.zh: 十二月，王仙芝寇沂州，平盧節度使宋威表請以歩騎五千別爲一使，兼帥本道兵所在討賊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Wang Xianzhi raided Yizhou; Pinglu Military Commissioner Song Wei submitted a memorial requesting five thousand infantry and cavalry be set apart as a separate command, and that he additionally lead his circuit's troops wherever needed to suppress bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Wang Xianzhi attacked Yizhou. Pinglu Military Commissioner Song Wei asked that five thousand foot and horse soldiers be set under a separate command, with himself leading his circuit's troops wherever bandits appeared.

sentences.zh: 乃以威爲諸道行營招討草賊使，仍給禁兵三千、甲騎五百。

translations.literal: Song Wei was then made Bandit-Suppression Commissioner for the Combined Circuits Field Headquarters, and additionally given three thousand palace troops and five hundred armored cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wei was appointed bandit-suppression commissioner for the combined field headquarters, with three thousand palace troops and five hundred armored cavalry added to his command.

sentences.zh: 因詔河南方鎭所遣討賊都頭-{並}-取威處分。

translations.literal: Accordingly an edict ordered that all bandit-hunting squad leaders dispatched by the Henan circuits take their orders from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: every bandit-hunting detachment leader sent by the Henan circuits was to obey Song Wei's command.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，天平軍奏遣將士張晏等救沂州，還，至義橋，聞北境-{復}-有盜起，留使扞-{御}-。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Tianping army reported that it had dispatched officers and soldiers Zhang Yan and others to relieve Yizhou; on their return, reaching Yiqiao, they heard bandits had risen again on the northern frontier and were ordered to stay and defend.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring the Tianping army reported that Zhang Yan and other officers had marched to relieve Yizhou. On the return march they reached Yiqiao, heard that bandits had risen again on the northern frontier, and were ordered to stay and hold the line.

sentences.zh: 晏等不從，喧噪趣鄆州。

translations.literal: Yan and the others disobeyed, clamoring noisily and pressing toward Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan and his men refused. They raised a tumult and marched on Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 都將張思泰、李承祐走馬出城，裂袖與盟，以俸錢備酒餚慰諭，然-{後}-定。

translations.literal: Commanders Zhang Sitai and Li Chengyou galloped out of the city, tore their sleeves to seal an oath, used their salary funds to prepare wine and food to comfort and persuade them, and only then were things settled.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders Zhang Sitai and Li Chengyou rode out of the city, tore their sleeves to bind an oath, bought wine and food from their own pay to soothe the men, and only then restored order.

sentences.zh: 語本軍宣慰一切，無得窮詰。

translations.literal: They ordered the army to announce comfort on all points and forbade exhaustive interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: They told the army that all grievances would be addressed and that no one was to be pressed for answers.

sentences.zh: 二月，敕福建、江西、湖南諸道觀察、刺史，皆訓練士卒。

translations.literal: In the second month, an edict ordered the observation commissioners and prefects of Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, and other circuits all to drill their soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month an edict ordered observation commissioners and prefects throughout Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, and neighboring circuits to drill their troops.

sentences.zh: 又令天下鄕邨各置弓刀鼓板以備群盜。

translations.literal: It further ordered every village and hamlet in the empire to keep bows, blades, drums, and clappers to guard against bandit gangs.
translations.idiomatic: Villages across the empire were also ordered to keep bows, blades, drums, and clappers against bandit raids.

sentences.zh: 賜兗海節度號泰-{寧}-軍。

translations.literal: The Yanhai command was granted the designation Taining Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Yanhai command was redesignated the Taining Army.

sentences.zh: 三月，盧龍節度使李茂勳請以其子幽州左司馬可舉知留-{後}-，自求致仕。

translations.literal: In the third month, Lulong Military Commissioner Li Maoxun requested that his son, Left Staff Officer of Youzhou Li Keju, be made acting governor, and that he himself be allowed to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Lulong Military Commissioner Li Maoxun asked that his son, Youzhou left staff officer Li Keju, be named acting governor while he himself retired from office.

sentences.zh: 詔茂勳以左-{僕}-射致仕，以可舉爲盧龍留-{後}-。

translations.literal: An edict allowed Maoxun to retire as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Keju was made acting governor of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted Maoxun retirement with the rank of left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and made Keju acting governor of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎、同平章事崔彦昭罷爲太子太傅。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Chancellery and Concurrent Grand Councillor Cui Yanzhao was removed and made Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Vice director of the chancellery and grand councillor Cui Yanzhao was dismissed and made grand tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 以左-{僕}-射王鐸兼門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Wang Duo was additionally made Vice Director of the Chancellery and Concurrent Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Left vice director Wang Duo was appointed vice director of the chancellery and grand councillor as well.

sentences.zh: 南詔遣使者詣髙駢求和而盜邊不息，駢斬其使者。

translations.literal: Nanzhao sent envoys to Gao Pian seeking peace, yet border raids did not cease; Pian executed the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao sent envoys to Gao Pian suing for peace, yet raids on the frontier never stopped. Pian had the envoys executed.

sentences.zh: 蠻之陷交趾也，虜安南經略判官杜驤妻李瑤。

translations.literal: When the barbarians captured Jiaozhi, they took as captive Li Yao, wife of Du Xiang, adjutant of the Annan pacification commission.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians seized Jiaozhi, they captured Li Yao, wife of Du Xiang, adjutant on the Annan pacification staff.

sentences.zh: 瑤，宗室之疎屬也。

translations.literal: Yao was a distant member of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was a distant kinswoman of the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 蠻遣瑤還，遞木夾以遺駢，稱「督爽牒西川節度使」，辭極驕慢。

translations.literal: The barbarians sent Yao back, delivering by relay wooden plaques to give to Pian, styled "Supervising Clerk memorializing the Military Commissioner of Sichuan"—the language extremely arrogant and insolent.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians sent Yao back with relayed wooden plaques addressed to Pian as "Supervising Clerk to the Military Commissioner of Sichuan"—language flagrantly insolent.

sentences.zh: 駢送瑤京師。

translations.literal: Pian sent Yao to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Pian sent Yao to the capital.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，-{復}-牒南詔，數其負累聖恩德、暴犯邊境、殘賊欺詐之罪，安南、大渡覆敗之狀，折辱之。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, he again sent a memorial to Nanzhao, recounting its crimes of ingratitude for accumulated imperial grace, violent border incursions, savage treachery and deceit, and the disasters at Annan and the Dadu River, shaming and humiliating them.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Gao Pian sent another dispatch to Nanzhao, listing its ingratitude for imperial favor, its violent border raids, its savage fraud, and the disasters at Annan and the Dadu River—and heaped humiliation upon it.

sentences.zh: 原州刺史史懷操貪暴，夏，四月，軍亂，逐之。

translations.literal: Yuanzhou Prefect Shi Huaicao was greedy and brutal; in summer, the fourth month, the army mutinied and drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhou prefect Shi Huaicao was greedy and brutal. In the fourth month of summer the garrison mutinied and expelled him.

sentences.zh: 賜宣武、感化節度、泗州防-{禦}-使密詔，選精兵數百人-{於}-巡内-{游}-奕，防衞綱船，五日一具上供錢米平安狀聞奏。

translations.literal: Secret edicts were granted to the Xuanwu and Ganhua military commissioners and the Sizhou defense commissioner, ordering selection of several hundred elite troops to patrol within the circuit and guard the tribute-shipping convoys; every five days a report on the safety of tribute funds and grain was to be submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Secret edicts went to the Xuanwu and Ganhua military commissioners and the Sizhou defense commissioner, ordering several hundred picked troops to patrol the interior routes and guard the tribute convoys. Every five days they were to file a report certifying the safe passage of tribute funds and grain.

sentences.zh: 五月，昭王汭薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Prince Zhao Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Prince Zhao Wei died.

sentences.zh: 以盧龍留-{後}-李可舉爲節度使。

translations.literal: Lulong Acting Governor Li Keju was made Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keju, acting governor of Lulong, was confirmed as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六月，撫王紘薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Prince Fu Hong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Prince Fu Hong died.

sentences.zh: 雄州地震裂，水湧，壞州城及公私戸-{捨}-倶盡。

translations.literal: Xiongzhou's earth quaked and split; water surged forth, destroying the prefectural city and all public and private dwellings completely.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongzhou was struck by earthquake and fissure; water gushed up and destroyed the prefectural seat and every public and private building.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以前巖州刺史髙傑爲左驍衞將軍，充縁海水軍都知兵馬使，以討王郢。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, former Yanzhou Prefect Gao Jie was made General of the Left Obedient Cavalry Guard and appointed Overall Commander of Coastal Naval Forces to campaign against Wang Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, former Yanzhou prefect Gao Jie was made general of the Left Obedient Cavalry Guard and overall commander of coastal naval forces to campaign against Wang Ying.

sentences.zh: 鄂王潤薨。

translations.literal: Prince E Run died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince E Run died.

sentences.zh: 加魏博節度使韓簡同平章事。

translations.literal: Weibo Military Commissioner Han Jian was given the additional title Concurrent Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Weibo Military Commissioner Han Jian was made concurrent grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 宋威撃王仙芝-{於}-沂州城下，大破之，仙芝亡去。

translations.literal: Song Wei struck Wang Xianzhi below the walls of Yizhou and routed him utterly; Xianzhi fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wei routed Wang Xianzhi beneath the walls of Yizhou. Xianzhi fled the field.

sentences.zh: 威奏仙芝已死，縱遣諸道兵，身還靑州。

translations.literal: Wei reported that Xianzhi was already dead, dismissed the troops from the various circuits, and himself returned to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wei reported that Xianzhi was dead, sent the allied contingents home, and returned himself to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 百官皆入賀。

translations.literal: All the civil and military officials entered court to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court turned out to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 居三日，州縣奏仙芝尚在，攻剽如故。

translations.literal: After three days, prefectures and counties reported that Xianzhi was still alive and attacking and plundering as before.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later prefectures and counties reported that Xianzhi was still alive and raiding as before.

sentences.zh: 時兵始休，詔-{復}--{發}-之，士皆忿怨思亂。

translations.literal: The troops had just been stood down; an edict ordered them dispatched again; the soldiers all nursed anger and resentment and thought of mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: The troops had only just been stood down when an edict sent them out again. Resentment spread through the ranks, and men talked of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 八月，仙芝陷陽翟、郟城，詔忠武節度使崔安潛-{發}-兵撃之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Xianzhi captured Yangdi and Jia Cheng; an edict ordered Zhongwu Military Commissioner Cui Anqian to dispatch troops to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Xianzhi seized Yangdi and Jia Cheng. The court ordered Zhongwu Military Commissioner Cui Anqian to march against him.

sentences.zh: 安潛，愼由之弟也。

translations.literal: Anqian was the younger brother of Shenyou.
translations.idiomatic: Anqian was the younger brother of Cui Shenyou.

sentences.zh: 又命昭義節度使曹翔將歩騎五千及義成兵衞東都宮，以左散騎常侍曾元裕爲招討副使，守東都，又詔山南東道節度使李福選歩騎二千守汝、鄧要路。

translations.literal: Cao Xiang, Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi, was further ordered to lead five thousand infantry and cavalry plus Yicheng troops to guard the Eastern Capital palace; Left Regular Attendant Zeng Yuanyu was made Deputy Bandit-Suppression Commissioner to hold the Eastern Capital; and an edict further ordered Shannan East Circuit Military Commissioner Li Fu to select two thousand infantry and cavalry to guard the strategic routes at Ru and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi Military Commissioner Cao Xiang was ordered to lead five thousand foot and horse soldiers plus Yicheng troops to guard the Eastern Capital palace. Left Regular Attendant Zeng Yuanyu was named deputy bandit-suppression commissioner to hold Luoyang. Shannan East Circuit Military Commissioner Li Fu was told to post two thousand foot and horse troops on the vital roads through Ru and Deng.

sentences.zh: 仙芝進逼汝州，詔邠-{寧}-節度使李侃、鳳翔節度使令狐綯選歩兵一千、騎兵五百守陝州、潼關。

translations.literal: Xianzhi pressed forward toward Ruzhou; an edict ordered Binning Military Commissioner Li Kan and Fengxiang Military Commissioner Linghu Tao to select one thousand infantry and five hundred cavalry to guard Shazhou and Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: As Xianzhi advanced on Ruzhou, Binning Military Commissioner Li Kan and Fengxiang Military Commissioner Linghu Tao were ordered to post one thousand infantry and five hundred cavalry at Shazhou and Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 加成德節度使王景崇兼中書令。

translations.literal: Chengde Military Commissioner Wang Jingchong was given the additional title Concurrent Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Chengde Military Commissioner Wang Jingchong was made concurrent chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day of the month (yihai), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the first day (yihai), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 丙子，王仙芝陷汝州，執刺史王鐐。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Wang Xianzhi captured Ruzhou and seized Prefect Wang Liao.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day Wang Xianzhi took Ruzhou and captured Prefect Wang Liao.

sentences.zh: 鐐，鐸之從父兄弟也。

translations.literal: Liao was a paternal cousin of Duo.
translations.idiomatic: Liao was a paternal cousin of Wang Duo.

sentences.zh: 東都大震，士民挈家逃出城。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital was greatly shaken; officials and commoners took their families and fled out of the city.
