translations.idiomatic: Panic seized Luoyang. Officials and townspeople fled the city with their families.

sentences.zh: 乙酉敕王仙芝、尚君長罪，除官，以招諭之。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou an edict pardoned the crimes of Wang Xianzhi and Shang Junzhang, cleared their offices, and sought to win them over by persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day an edict pardoned Wang Xianzhi and Shang Junzhang, cleared their records, and offered them official posts to bring them in.

sentences.zh: 仙芝陷陽武，攻鄭州，昭義監軍判官雷殷符屯中牟，撃仙芝，破走之。

translations.literal: Xianzhi captured Yangwu and attacked Zhengzhou; Zhaoyi Army Supervisor Adjutant Lei Yinfu encamped at Zhongmou, struck Xianzhi, and routed and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi seized Yangwu and attacked Zhengzhou. Zhaoyi army supervisor adjutant Lei Yinfu encamped at Zhongmou, struck Xianzhi, and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，仙芝南攻唐、鄧。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Xianzhi attacked south toward Tang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Xianzhi turned south to attack Tang and Deng.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使髙駢-{築}-成都羅城，使僧景仙規度，週二十五-{里}-，悉召縣令庀徒賦役，吏受百錢以上皆死。

translations.literal: Sichuan Military Commissioner Gao Pian built Chengdu's outer city ramparts, had the monk Jing Xian survey and plan them, with a circumference of twenty-five li; he summoned all prefects to organize labor corvée; any clerk who accepted more than a hundred cash was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan Military Commissioner Gao Pian built Chengdu's outer ramparts. Monk Jing Xian laid out a circuit twenty-five li around. Every prefect was summoned to levy labor. Any clerk who took so much as a hundred cash in bribes was executed.

sentences.zh: 蜀土疎惡，以甓甃之，還城十-{里}-内取土，皆劃丘垤平之，無得爲坎埳以害耕-{種}-；

translations.literal: Sichuan's soil was loose and poor; he lined it with brick; within ten li of the returned city wall, earth was taken and every mound and hummock leveled flat, not allowed to become pits and trenches that would harm farming;
translations.idiomatic: The soil of Shu was loose and poor, so he faced the walls with brick. Earth for the work was taken within ten li of the city, every mound scraped level so that no pit would scar the fields;

sentences.zh: 役者不過十日而代，衆樂其均，不費撲撻而功辦。

translations.literal: Corvée laborers served no more than ten days before replacement; the masses rejoiced at the fairness; without wasting beatings the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: No laborer served more than ten days before relief; the people welcomed the fair rotation, and the work finished without a lash being wasted.

sentences.zh: 自八月癸-{丑}--{築}-之，至十一月戊子畢功。

translations.literal: From the eighth month on the day guichou building began, until the eleventh month on the day wuzi the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Construction began on guichou day in the eighth month and was finished on wuzi day in the eleventh.

sentences.zh: 役之始作也，駢恐南詔揚聲入寇，雖不敢決來，役者必驚擾，乃奏遣景仙-{托}--{遊}-行入南詔，説諭驃信使歸附中國，仍許妻以公主，因與議二國禮儀，久之不決。

translations.literal: When the corvée work first began, Pian feared Nanzhao would loudly proclaim an invasion; though they might not dare certainly to come, the laborers would surely be alarmed and disturbed; he therefore memorialized dispatching Jing Xian on a feigned tour into Nanzhao to persuade the Piao Xin to return and attach to China, furthermore promising marriage to a princess, and thereby discussing the two states' ceremonial protocols—long unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: When the work began, Pian feared Nanzhao would trumpet an invasion. Even if the barbarians hesitated to strike, the laborers would panic. He memorialized sending Jing Xian on a pretended mission into Nanzhao to persuade the Piao Xin to submit, promising a princess in marriage and negotiating state protocol—talk that dragged on without result.

sentences.zh: 駢又聲言欲巡邊，朝夕通烽火，至大渡河，而實不行，蠻中惴恐。

translations.literal: Pian also declared he wished to tour the frontier, beacons flashed morning and evening as far as the Dadu River, yet in fact he did not go; among the barbarians fear and dread mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Pian also declared he would tour the frontier. Beacons flashed day and night as far as the Dadu River, though he never marched. Fear spread through the barbarian camps.

sentences.zh: 由是訖-{於}-城成，邊候無風塵之警。

translations.literal: From this until the walls were completed, frontier scouts had no alarms of war dust.
translations.idiomatic: Until the walls stood complete, frontier pickets saw no sign of raiders.

sentences.zh: 先是，西川將吏入南詔，驃信皆坐受其拜，駢以其俗尚浮屠，故遣景仙往，驃信果帥其大臣迎拜，信用其言。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sichuan generals and officials entered Nanzhao, the Piao Xin always sat and received their bows; Pian, knowing their custom revered Buddhism, therefore sent Jing Xian; the Piao Xin indeed led his great ministers out to welcome and bow, and trusted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, when Sichuan officers entered Nanzhao, the Piao Xin had always sat and received their bows. Knowing the Nanzhao revered Buddhism, Pian sent the monk Jing Xian. The Piao Xin led his ministers out to welcome and bow to him, and took his words to heart.

sentences.zh: 王仙芝攻郢、-{復}-二州，陷之。

translations.literal: Wang Xianzhi attacked the two prefectures of Ying and Fu and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianzhi attacked Ying and Fu and captured both.

sentences.zh: 王郢因温州刺史魯寔請降，寔屢爲之論奏，敕郢詣闕。

translations.literal: Wang Ying, through Wenzhou Prefect Lu Shi, requested surrender; Shi repeatedly memorialized on his behalf; an edict ordered Ying to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying asked to surrender through Wenzhou prefect Lu Shi, who memorialized repeatedly on his behalf. The court ordered Ying to present himself at the capital.

sentences.zh: 郢擁兵遷延，半年不至，固求望海鎭使；

translations.literal: Ying held his troops and delayed; half a year passed without his arrival; he obstinately requested the post of Wanghaitown commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Ying kept his army and delayed. Half a year passed without his coming. He stubbornly demanded the post of Wanghaitown commissioner;

sentences.zh: 朝廷不許，以郢爲右率府率，仍令左神策軍補以重職，其先所掠之財，-{並}-令給與。

translations.literal: The court did not agree; Ying was made Captain of the Right Guard; the Left Divine Strategy Army was further ordered to supplement him with a heavy post; all wealth he had previously plundered was likewise ordered returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused. Ying was made captain of the Right Guard, with the Left Divine Strategy Army to supply him a substantive post. Even the loot he had taken was ordered returned to him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，王仙芝攻申、光、廬、壽、舒、通等州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Wang Xianzhi attacked the prefectures of Shen, Guang, Lu, Shou, Shu, and Tong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Wang Xianzhi attacked Shen, Guang, Lu, Shou, Shu, and Tong.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使劉鄴奏求益兵，敕感化節度使薛能選精兵數千助之。

translations.literal: Huainan Military Commissioner Liu Ye memorialized requesting additional troops; an edict ordered Ganhua Military Commissioner Xue Neng to select several thousand elite troops to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan Military Commissioner Liu Ye asked for reinforcements. The court ordered Ganhua Military Commissioner Xue Neng to send several thousand picked troops to his aid.

sentences.zh: 鄭畋以言計不行，稱疾遜位，不許，乃上言：「自沂州奏捷之-{後}-，仙芝愈肆猖狂，屠陷五六州，瘡痍數千-{里}-。

translations.literal: Zheng Tian, because his proposals went unheeded, claimed illness and requested to step down; this was not permitted; he then submitted a memorial: "Since the report of victory at Yizhou, Xianzhi has grown ever more wildly arrogant, slaughtering and capturing five or six prefectures, leaving wounds across thousands of li.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tian, frustrated that his counsel went unheeded, pleaded illness and asked to resign. When the court refused, he memorialized: "Since Song Wei's false victory at Yizhou, Xianzhi has grown ever bolder. He has sacked five or six prefectures and laid waste to thousands of li of countryside.

sentences.zh: 宋威衰老多病，自妄奏以來，諸道尤所不服，今淹留毫州，殊無進討之意。

translations.literal: Song Wei is aged and infirm with many illnesses; since his false memorial, the various circuits especially will not submit to him; now he lingers at Bozhou with no intent whatsoever to advance and suppress.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wei is old and sick. Since his false report of victory the allied circuits trust him even less. He now sits idle at Bozhou with no appetite for pursuit.

sentences.zh: 曾元裕擁兵蘄、黃，專慾望風退縮。

translations.literal: Zeng Yuanyu holds troops at Qí and Huang, devoted only to watching the wind and shrinking back.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Yuanyu sits with his army at Qí and Huang, ready to flee at the first sign of trouble.

sentences.zh: 若使賊陷揚州，則江南亦非國有。

translations.literal: If the bandits should capture Yangzhou, then the lands south of the Yangtze would no longer belong to the state.
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels take Yangzhou, the entire lower Yangtze will be lost to the throne.

sentences.zh: 崔安潛威望過人，張自勉驍雄良將，宮苑使李晟，西平王晟之孫，嚴而有勇。

translations.literal: Cui Anqian's prestige surpasses other men; Zhang Zimian is a fierce and excellent general; Palace Commissioner Li Zhuan, grandson of Western Pacification King Li Sheng, is stern and brave.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Anqian's authority outmatches any rival. Zhang Zimian is a proven fighter. Palace Commissioner Li Zhuan, grandson of the Western Pacification King Li Sheng, is stern and fearless.

sentences.zh: 請以安潛爲行營都統，瑑爲招討使代威，自勉爲副使代元裕。」

translations.literal: I request that Anqian be made Overall Commander of the Field Headquarters, Zhuan be made Bandit-Suppression Commissioner in Wei's place, and Zimian be made Deputy Commissioner in Yuanyu's place."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Cui Anqian be made overall field commander, Li Zhuan bandit-suppression commissioner in Song Wei's place, and Zhang Zimian deputy commissioner in Zeng Yuanyu's place."

sentences.zh: 上頗采其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor largely adopted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely adopted his advice.

sentences.zh: 靑、滄軍士戍安南，還至桂州，逐觀察使李瓚。

translations.literal: Soldiers of Qing and Cang, garrisoned in Annan, upon returning reached Guizhou and drove out Observation Commissioner Li Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from Qing and Cang, returning from garrison duty in Annan, reached Guizhou and expelled Observation Commissioner Li Zan.

sentences.zh: 瓚，宗閔之子也。

translations.literal: Zan was the son of Zongmin.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was a son of Li Zongmin.

sentences.zh: 以右諫議大夫張禹謨爲桂州觀察使。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Grandee Zhang Yumo was made Observation Commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Right remonstrance grandee Zhang Yumo was appointed observation commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 桂管監軍李維周驕橫，瓚-{曲}-奉之，浸不能-{制}-。

translations.literal: Guì Circuit Army Supervisor Li Weizhou was arrogant and overbearing; Zan catered to him with deference and gradually could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou circuit army supervisor Li Weizhou was insufferably arrogant. Li Zan indulged him until he could no longer keep him in check.

sentences.zh: 桂管有兵八百人，防-{禦}-使-{才}-得百人，-{餘}-皆屬監軍。

translations.literal: Guì Circuit had eight hundred troops; the defense commissioner controlled only one hundred; the remainder all belonged to the army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: The Guizhou garrison numbered eight hundred men. The defense commissioner controlled only a hundred; the rest answered to the army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 又預-{於}-逐帥之謀，強取兩使印，擅補知州官，奪昭州送使錢。

translations.literal: He further participated in the plot to drive out the commander, forcibly seized the seals of both commissioners, arbitrarily appointed acting prefects, and seized Zhaozhou's tribute-envoy funds.
translations.idiomatic: He had helped plot the expulsion of Li Zan, seized both commissioners' seals, appointed prefects on his own authority, and diverted Zhaozhou's tribute-envoy funds.

sentences.zh: 詔禹謨-{並}-按之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yumo to investigate all of this jointly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zhang Yumo to investigate the entire affair.

sentences.zh: 禹謨，徹之子也。

translations.literal: Yumo was the son of Che.
translations.idiomatic: Yumo was a son of Zhang Che.

sentences.zh: 招討副使、都監楊-{復}-光奏尚君長弟讓據査牙山，官軍退保鄧州。

translations.literal: Deputy Bandit-Suppression Commissioner and Overall Supervisor Yang Fuguang reported that Shang Junzhang's younger brother Rang held Chaya Mountain; government troops withdrew to hold Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy bandit-suppression commissioner and overall supervisor Yang Fuguang reported that Shang Junzhang's brother Rang held Chaya Mountain and that imperial troops had fallen back to Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: -{復}-光，玄-{價}-之養子也。

translations.literal: Fuguang was the adopted son of Xuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang was the adopted son of Yang Xuanjia.

sentences.zh: 王仙芝攻蘄州，蘄州刺史裴渥，王鐸知舉時所擢進士也。

translations.literal: Wang Xianzhi attacked Qízhou; Qízhou Prefect Pei Wo was a jinshi elevated when Wang Duo was chief examiner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianzhi attacked Qí Prefecture. Prefect Pei Wo had been a jinshi candidate Wang Duo had passed when chief examiner.

sentences.zh: 王鐐在賊中，爲仙芝以書説渥。

translations.literal: Wang Liao was among the bandits; he wrote on Xianzhi's behalf to persuade Wo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liao, still captive among the rebels, wrote on Xianzhi's behalf to persuade Pei Wo.

sentences.zh: 渥與仙芝約，斂兵不戰，許爲之奏官；

translations.literal: Wo made a pact with Xianzhi to keep his troops quiet and not fight, promising to memorialize requesting an office for him;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Wo agreed with Xianzhi to stand his troops down and promised to petition for an official post;

sentences.zh: 鐐亦説仙芝許以如約。

translations.literal: Liao also persuaded Xianzhi to promise to abide by the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liao likewise persuaded Xianzhi to honor the bargain.

sentences.zh: 渥乃開城延仙芝及黃巣輩三十-{餘}-人入城，置酒，大陳貨賄以贈之，表陳其狀。

translations.literal: Wo then opened the city and invited Xianzhi and more than thirty men including Huang Chao and his band into the city, set out wine, lavishly displayed goods and bribes to present to them, and submitted a memorial stating the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Wo opened the gates and welcomed Xianzhi and more than thirty followers, including Huang Chao, into the city. He feasted them, heaped gifts upon them, and memorialized the court with the full account.

sentences.zh: 諸宰相多言：「先帝不赦龐勳，期年卒誅之。

translations.literal: Many among the chief ministers said: "The former Emperor did not pardon Pang Xun; within a year he was finally executed.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the chief ministers objected: "The late emperor refused to pardon Pang Xun, and within a year Pang was killed.

sentences.zh: 今仙芝小賊，非龐勳之比，赦罪除官，益長-{奸}-宄。」

translations.literal: Now Xianzhi is a petty bandit, no match for Pang Xun; pardoning his crimes and clearing his office will only further feed treachery and villainy."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi is a petty outlaw, no Pang Xun. To pardon him and grant office would only embolden every rogue in the empire."

sentences.zh: 王鐸固請，許之。

translations.literal: Wang Duo firmly petitioned; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo pressed hard, and the court relented.

sentences.zh: 乃以仙芝爲左神策軍押牙兼監察-{御}-史，遣中使以告身即蘄州授之。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was then made Adjutant of the Left Divine Strategy Army and Concurrent Investigating Censor; a palace envoy was dispatched to confer the commission letter right at Qízhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was appointed adjutant of the Left Divine Strategy Army with concurrent rank as investigating censor, and a palace envoy was sent to Qí Prefecture to deliver his commission on the spot.

sentences.zh: 仙芝得之甚喜，鐐、渥皆賀。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was greatly pleased to receive it; Liao and Wo both offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was overjoyed. Wang Liao and Pei Wo both congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 未退，黃巣以官不及己，大怒曰：「始者共立大誓，橫行天下，今獨取官赴左軍，使此五千-{餘}-衆安所歸乎！」

translations.literal: Before they had withdrawn, Huang Chao, because the office did not extend to him, raged in great anger: "At the start we together made a great oath to rampage across the empire—now he alone takes an office and goes to the Left Army. Where are these five thousand-odd followers to go!"
translations.idiomatic: Before the party broke up, Huang Chao—passed over for any post—exploded in fury: "We swore together to sweep the empire. Now you take a commission for yourself and march into the Left Army. What becomes of the five thousand men who rode with us?"

sentences.zh: 因毆仙芝，傷其首，其衆喧噪不已。

translations.literal: Thereupon he beat Xianzhi, wounding his head; his followers clamored without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Xianzhi and bloodied his head. The rebels roared in uproar.

sentences.zh: 仙芝畏衆怒，遂不受命。

translations.literal: Xianzhi feared the crowd's wrath and thereupon did not accept the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful of the mutiny, Xianzhi refused the commission.

sentences.zh: 大掠蘄州，城中之人，半驅半殺，焚其廬-{舍}-。

translations.literal: They plundered Qizhou on a great scale; of the people in the city, half were driven off and half were killed, and their houses were burned.
translations.idiomatic: They sacked Qizhou wholesale—half the townspeople were driven away, half slaughtered, and their homes put to the torch.

sentences.zh: 渥奔鄂州，敕使奔襄州，鐐爲賊所拘。

translations.literal: Wo fled to Ezhou, the imperial envoy fled to Xiangzhou, and Liao was seized by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Wo fled to Ezhou, the imperial envoy to Xiangzhou, and Liao was taken prisoner by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊乃分其軍三千-{餘}-人從仙芝及尚君長，二千-{餘}-人從巣，各分道而去。

translations.literal: The rebels then divided their army: more than three thousand followed Xianzhi and Shang Junzhang, and more than two thousand followed Chao; each column went its separate way.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then split their forces—more than three thousand went with Xianzhi and Shang Junzhang, more than two thousand with Huang Chao—and marched off on separate roads.
